<a id="phase-44-boundaries-and-guardrails"></a>

#### Boundaries and guardrails

No replacing Supabase Auth, bypassing Phase 12, trusting group names, merging by email, sharing credentials, automatically granting broad membership, or copying an IdP directory into the CRM as a new system of record. No public account enumeration through domain discovery or provider errors. No tenant-wide social-login toggle presented as enterprise SSO. Directory provision/deprovision does not create marketing consent, a missionary appointment, a care determination, compensation/payee authority, donor authority or a financial write.

**Only the explicitly adopted SSO and provisioning successors activate.** Reserved nested groups, arbitrary ABAC conditions, bulk permission widening, unrelated NHI sender constraints and enterprise commercial features stay under their existing owners and activation rules. This phase must not quietly implement all the reserved fields in issue #686. Recovery does not grant access to sealed care or bypass an independent financial approval.

**Protective behavior is not optional automation.** Validated deactivation cannot depend on an enabled Workflow Studio template or wait for a staffing handoff. Manual ordinary group changes, directory changes and protected emergency changes must converge through the same grant-state owner, with their distinct required authority. Retain old-generation inertness tests alongside new qualified-profile tests; do not simply disable assertSsoInert or remove identity-change safety fixtures globally.

<a id="phase-44-acceptance-and-release"></a>

#### Acceptance and release

**All cases are specified, not executed.** Demonstrate real provider behavior in controlled test tenants and the actual authenticated application/database stack. Source code, green documentation checks or a successful vendor-console login are insufficient. Record supported provider plans, metadata/profile versions, schemas, credential custody, exact identity-transition policy and evidence for each completed profile.

| **Case** | **Required observable proof** |
| --- | --- |
| EID-AT-01 | The Phase 12 reserved generation remains inert for sign-in/provision-up while its qualified active=false safety adapter still works independently. |
| EID-AT-02 | One adopted enterprise profile cannot activate a different protocol, nested groups, ABAC, tenant provisioning or another tenant's connection. |
| EID-AT-03 | A real administrator configures and tests the correct tenant/provider; spoofed domains, posted provider IDs and wrong-account control cannot bind. |
| EID-AT-04 | Hostile metadata, private-network URLs, invalid trust, replayed assertions, expired signatures and audience/recipient mismatches fail safely. |
| EID-AT-05 | Application-initiated SAML and an IdP bookmark through that path preserve PKCE and the approved redirect without a separate app-local auth client. |
| EID-AT-06 | Verified provider/session evidence binds the correct principal and tenant; user metadata, email domain, role label and array ordering cannot grant access. |
| EID-AT-07 | A new authenticated but unadmitted identity has no operational permissions; any permitted starter uses the current approved membership command. |
| EID-AT-08 | Required SSO applies across relevant protected app routes and existing sessions; an old password/social token or alternate callback cannot bypass it. |
| EID-AT-09 | Existing regular and SSO accounts sharing an email require the approved proof/binding transition; they do not silently merge or union grants. |
| EID-AT-10 | Identity/email succession preserves attribution, protects financial history and suspends/re-attests sensitive grants under the predecessor contract. |
| EID-AT-11 | Concurrent first login, SCIM creation, repeated callback and response loss converge on one source binding without duplicate privileged accounts. |
| EID-AT-12 | Partial external-auth creation before local acceptance remains unentitled and recoverable; an orphaned provider account cannot acquire authority. |
| EID-AT-13 | The real selected IdP completes supported SCIM discovery, lookup, create, update and PATCH cases with correct resource and error semantics. |
| EID-AT-14 | Credential/body/path scope mismatch, cross-tenant external IDs, token replay after rotation and unbounded/hostile filters cannot enumerate or mutate. |
| EID-AT-15 | Null/omitted/removed attributes, case rules, pagination and supported version conditions match the declared profile; unsupported operations never report false success. |
| EID-AT-16 | Stable external group IDs map only to approved flat groups; a rename, recycled name, nested group or forged claim cannot expand permissions. |
| EID-AT-17 | Removing a mapping removes its attributable membership effect without erasing unrelated grants; the existing privacy/purpose/entity floors still subtract. |
| EID-AT-18 | Directory changes cannot self-approve clearance, sensitive elevation, named care access or a financial operation through a friendly group label. |
| EID-AT-19 | Received active=false denies applicable tenant assignments within the existing Phase 12 enforcement bound and invalidates protected streams and queued user authority. |
| EID-AT-20 | Deactivate → reactivate → deactivate is processed correctly; duplicate old messages and stale positive updates cannot swallow the second revocation. |
| EID-AT-21 | Certificate rotation, expired metadata and issuer/provider replacement use exact reviewed trust generations; no unrelated tenant is changed. |
| EID-AT-22 | Unmatched deactivation is durably visible, repairable and fences a later first login/create; valid negative security events are not delayed by optional workflow or campaign limits. |
| EID-AT-23 | SCIM deletion/deactivation in tenant A does not delete Party/gifts or tenant B authority; any broader provider reauthentication effect is accurately disclosed. |
| EID-AT-24 | Required assurance and step-up are actually proved; SSO, asserted MFA, SMS availability and provider logout cannot substitute for local authorization. |
| EID-AT-25 | A tested authorized administrator recovery works during IdP failure without a permanent shared bypass or automatic sealed-data access. |
| EID-AT-26 | Last-owner protection and legitimate emergency/deprovisioning follow the approved owner policy; unsafe access is not retained silently for convenience. |
| EID-AT-27 | Incomplete directory snapshots, provider silence, removed scope and upstream deletion quarantine remain visible uncertainty, not mass local deletion. |
| EID-AT-28 | Reviewed mapping changes show exact impact; concurrent native edits or changed authorization invalidate stale plans instead of overwriting current grants. |
| EID-AT-29 | Disconnect/reconnect and provider transition fence old positive work, reject newly presented retired credentials, retain accepted safe revocation/recovery and do not automatically enable password fallback. |
| EID-AT-30 | Privacy and backup restore retain required minimal revocation/identity evidence without restoring deleted contents, old tokens or revoked memberships. |
| EID-AT-31 | A revoked workflow human owner cannot authorize a queued NHI action; no automation ownership or task responsibility transfers by directory inference. |
| EID-AT-32 | Legitimate organization-owned content appointments follow their source policy; directory changes cannot erase finance/care history or redirect money. |
| EID-AT-33 | Administrator and staff finish setup, sign-in, denied-access recovery and required migration using keyboard, screen reader and narrow-screen layouts. |
| EID-AT-34 | All selected Entra/Google sign-in and selected SCIM profiles complete the three checkpoints, production-shaped fault/load tests and documented user pilot. |

**Operating evidence.** Measure connection lookup, callback completion, concurrent sign-in/provisioning, directory batch size, largest group update, local revocation propagation, stream closure, reconciliation backlog and cross-tenant workload isolation. State source-event latency separately from received-to-denied latency. Approve the quantitative profile before testing and report observed results; do not invent a universal upstream synchronization SLA. Repeat the deactivate/reactivate cycle and old-session access attempt against the actual session and database implementation.

**Rollout and containment.** Release by exact tenant/connection/profile with a tested optional pilot before mandatory staff enforcement. Preserve a source-authorized recovery path, existing donor/public access and unrelated tenants. Shut down new positive federation/provisioning independently from required negative-event processing and recovery. Restore with favorable admission disabled until connection generations, identity bindings, revocations and memberships are reconciled. Retiring old trust or readers requires evidence that required sessions/history and recovery no longer depend on them.

**Runbooks.** Include failed setup, wrong-account login, an existing-account collision, unexpected JIT admission, invalid SCIM PATCH, group drift, unmatched leaver, delayed upstream deactivation, lost certificate, IdP outage, malicious metadata, compromised connector credential, last-owner loss and backup restore. Each names the responsible source owner, safe diagnostic evidence, exact supported operation and escalation. No runbook should repair by editing auth tables, deleting a Party or clearing a governance epoch manually.

<a id="phase-44-open-decisions"></a>

#### Open decisions

Resolve the exact Supabase project/plan/runtime cohort and provider profiles; SAML initiation and assurance evidence; existing-account binding/succession supported by Phase 4; pilot enforcement scope; whether bounded JIT admission is allowed; SCIM authentication and supported verbs/attributes/filter/PATCH/version behavior; immutable external identity source; group-mapping approval and provenance; lifecycle ordering/reactivation proof; provider-wide versus tenant-scoped session cleanup; certificate overlap/rotation; connection-owner departure; negative-event service authority; recovery personnel and procedure; retention/residency; and the approved quantitative load/revocation profile.

Each decision needs an accountable owner, concrete selected behavior, evidence and a safe unresolved state. Library/provider gaps must be resolved through the supported adapter or an explicit source-compatible successor before the affected required profile can close; a successful new-user demo cannot stand in for migration or deprovisioning. Do not promise unsupported SAML Single Logout, automatic account linking, arbitrary OIDC providers, every SCIM feature, or instantaneous receipt of upstream directory changes. Refresh current vendor and standards evidence at build and before activation. \[I-01–I-06\]

<a id="roadmap-recipe-register"></a>

### Workflow recipe register

These 96 recipes are part of the planned product. Their delivery phases are fixed below; exact business/source capability qualification remains mandatory. All optional starters install disabled. Enabling one requires current tenant authority, real bindings and an explicit view of the recipients, dates and effects. Protected coordination opens or requests the native owner operation rather than recreating its business decision.

Common timing and recovery: the source policy wins. Where permitted, the supplied starting proposal is three business days, no more than two optional outward reminders and internal escalation; approve concrete dates at tenant activation. Recurring/pledge eligibility and emergency care keep their own timing. Missing owners route only to an eligible source queue; unknown evidence/results block or reconcile; accepted source history remains intact. Visibility applies to each recipient purpose and all counts/logs. No raw source records are copied into workflow/email state.

Each recipe retains three acceptance cases: its source-backed outcome, an allowed configuration change that preserves the protected boundary, and replay/cancellation-race proof. Test IDs follow T-\[recipe ID\]-01, -02 and -03. Together with WS-AT-001–WS-AT-064 this is the 352-case source specification, not a report of executed product tests.

| **Delivery checkpoint** | **Phase** | **Recipe allocation** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| CORE | 34 | 57: ADM-01–10; GEN-01–09, 13–17, 19–20; DON-14–16; FIN-01–12; MPD-02–05, 07–08; COM-01–10. |
| MOBILIZATION | 41 | 12: MOB-01–12. Prioritized immediately after CORE. |
| GIVING | 35 | 15: DON-01–13; MPD-01 and MPD-06. |
| EVENTS | 37 | 3: GEN-10–12. Selected application lanes also need exact Phase 41 services. |
| CARE | 38 | 9: CARE-01–08 and GEN-18. |
| FULL | — | All 96 plus their applicable shared/source/lane evidence. Never a prerequisite of CORE. |

<a id="phase-44-adm-administration-and-operations"></a>

#### ADM — Administration and operations

<a id="roadmap-recipe-adm-01"></a>

##### ADM-01 — Staff onboarding  \|  Phase 34

**Start and process.** An authorized staff onboarding request is accepted. Confirm intended responsibilities → collect policy acknowledgments → request source-authorized access → assign orientation → verify receiving manager handoff.

**Controls.** Checklist, eligible role slots, orientation schedule, approved message. **Evidence.** Policy acknowledgments, role-request refs, orientation completion, handoff acceptance. **Boundary.** Access grants remain identity-owned and require independent current authorization.

<a id="roadmap-recipe-adm-02"></a>

##### ADM-02 — Responsibility change and handoff  \|  Phase 34

**Start and process.** A staff responsibility change is recorded. Inventory eligible open assignments → propose reassignment → request source access review → obtain receiving-owner acknowledgment.

**Controls.** Handoff checklist, reminders, eligible fallback team. **Evidence.** Source assignment versions and acknowledged handoff. **Boundary.** Relationship/assignment changes cannot create permission.

<a id="roadmap-recipe-adm-03"></a>

##### ADM-03 — Staff departure  \|  Phase 34

**Start and process.** A departure process is explicitly opened. Stop new assigned optional work → inventory automation ownership → request identity revocation → reassign source-owned work → review records and external sessions.

**Controls.** Due dates, responsible teams, exit checklist. **Evidence.** Confirmed revocation refs, reassignment results, unresolved exception list. **Boundary.** No automatic financial succession, care disclosure, or retention disposal.

<a id="roadmap-recipe-adm-04"></a>

##### ADM-04 — Template ownership and periodic review  \|  Phase 34

**Start and process.** An approved template review schedule becomes due. Check owner and dependencies → simulate proposed updates → route publication review → retain or retire future enrollment.

**Controls.** Review cadence, review team, checklist. **Evidence.** Review decision and publication/retirement reference. **Boundary.** Review completion cannot itself publish or change existing runs.

<a id="roadmap-recipe-adm-05"></a>

##### ADM-05 — Stalled workflow recovery  \|  Phase 34

**Start and process.** A source-qualified workflow attention event is recorded. Assign operator → inspect exact operation and source status → request safe reconciliation → verify source recovery.

**Controls.** Urgency within policy, eligible operator, escalation cadence. **Evidence.** Source recovery result or documented outstanding uncertainty. **Boundary.** No blind replay, invented success, or automatic skipping of required evidence.

<a id="roadmap-recipe-adm-06"></a>

##### ADM-06 — Tenant custom-record process  \|  Phase 34

**Start and process.** A permitted custom-record event or manual enrollment is accepted. Collect approved fields → assign human work → route on typed facts → request allowed custom-data commands → record declared result.

**Controls.** Allowed fields, role bindings, steps, conditions, bounded reminders. **Evidence.** Versioned form submissions, permitted custom commands, final process outcome. **Boundary.** Custom records cannot become financial, permission, or clinical shadow systems.

<a id="roadmap-recipe-adm-07"></a>

##### ADM-07 — Import review coordination  \|  Phase 34

**Start and process.** The import owner creates a review-ready manifest. Review mapping and exceptions → assign data-owner corrections → invoke authorized import acceptance → inspect source outcome.

**Controls.** Review owner, checklist, reminder dates. **Evidence.** Exact source manifest approval and import results. **Boundary.** Historical imported facts remain side-effect-dark; Studio cannot accept arbitrary raw records.

<a id="roadmap-recipe-adm-08"></a>

##### ADM-08 — Duplicate or incomplete data stewardship  \|  Phase 34

**Start and process.** A certified data-health rule produces a finding. Assign steward → inspect source evidence → propose correction or merge → use source-reviewed command → verify result.

**Controls.** Eligible finding classes, owner, review cadence. **Evidence.** Reviewed source correction/merge outcome. **Boundary.** No blind merge, invented profile facts, or financial history rewriting.

<a id="roadmap-recipe-adm-09"></a>

##### ADM-09 — Scheduled report coordination  \|  Phase 34

**Start and process.** An authorized source report schedule or request is accepted. Request source report generation → observe recipient-specific result → route failed delivery or access review.

**Controls.** Native source schedule, allowed recipients, report parameters. **Evidence.** Report run ref and separately recorded delivery/attention results. **Boundary.** Reporting owns schedule, filters, eligibility and source totals; no duplicate report timer.

<a id="roadmap-recipe-adm-10"></a>

##### ADM-10 — Integration health recovery  \|  Phase 34

**Start and process.** The connector owner reports drift, failure, or expired authorization. Route owner alert → open native reconnect/recovery → verify certified connection state → resume only affected safe work.

**Controls.** Owner, alert urgency, approved checklist. **Evidence.** Connector-owned recovery and per-operation result. **Boundary.** No pasted credentials, raw keys, blind provider switching, or unsafe replay.

<a id="phase-44-gen-common-operations-and-support-hub"></a>

#### GEN — Common operations and Support Hub

<a id="roadmap-recipe-gen-01"></a>

##### GEN-01 — Initial inquiry response  \|  Phase 34

**Start and process.** A valid inquiry is accepted through the source intake. Classify using permitted fields → assign responsible role → request acknowledgment → create discovery task → record next route.

**Controls.** Categories, role/fallback, acknowledgment, due date, follow-up. **Evidence.** Inquiry version, assignment, communication intent, discovery outcome. **Boundary.** Unknown or duplicate identity is not silently promoted to broad CRM access.

<a id="roadmap-recipe-gen-02"></a>

##### GEN-02 — Referral intake  \|  Phase 34

**Start and process.** A referral with permitted contact purpose is recorded. Review referral purpose and permission → assign follow-up → request appropriate contact → record accepted next action or expiry.

**Controls.** Questions, owner, permitted cadence, expiry. **Evidence.** Referral provenance, contact eligibility, follow-up outcome. **Boundary.** A referral does not imply marketing consent or record-sharing access.

<a id="roadmap-recipe-gen-03"></a>

##### GEN-03 — Missing profile information  \|  Phase 34

**Start and process.** A source-qualified completeness rule flags required data. Identify allowed missing fields → request information → review submission → invoke approved record update.

**Controls.** Permitted fields, responsible person, reminders. **Evidence.** Submitted answers and source update result. **Boundary.** Source-certified absence differs from unknown; no arbitrary profile overwrite.

<a id="roadmap-recipe-gen-04"></a>

##### GEN-04 — Contact-information change follow-up  \|  Phase 34

**Start and process.** Identity/CRM accepts a contact-change request. Observe source verification requirement → notify eligible owner → request permitted confirmation → record source completion.

**Controls.** Approved wording, staff task, allowable follow-up. **Evidence.** Identity-owned confirmation outcome. **Boundary.** Studio cannot replace verification, reveal account existence, or trust unverified destinations.

<a id="roadmap-recipe-gen-05"></a>

##### GEN-05 — Church or partner onboarding  \|  Phase 34

**Start and process.** A sending/supporting partner onboarding is opened. Assign relationship lead → collect organization contacts → schedule introductory work → request agreements → acknowledge handoff.

**Controls.** Required information, checklist, owner, review dates. **Evidence.** Partner contact refs, reviewed documents, handoff. **Boundary.** Organizational relationship does not grant member access or alter giving authorization.

<a id="roadmap-recipe-gen-06"></a>

##### GEN-06 — Document request and review  \|  Phase 34

**Start and process.** A source-approved document requirement is created. Request exact evidence → accept private upload → observe scan → route reviewer → accept correction or qualified evidence.

**Controls.** Document category, reviewer, deadline, reminders. **Evidence.** Private asset and exact acceptance decision. **Boundary.** Upload, clean scan, and accepted evidence remain distinct.

<a id="roadmap-recipe-gen-07"></a>

##### GEN-07 — Agreement signing coordination  \|  Phase 34

**Start and process.** A source agreement version requires signatures. Prepare exact approved document → request signatures through certified/manual path → wait for all required signers → record source completion.

**Controls.** Signer roles within source contract, order, reminders. **Evidence.** Document version, signer set, source signature evidence. **Boundary.** Old signatures cannot satisfy replaced documents; no certification claim from a manual scan.

<a id="roadmap-recipe-gen-08"></a>

##### GEN-08 — Training or policy acknowledgment  \|  Phase 34

**Start and process.** A source-owned requirement is assigned. Assign course/resource → request acknowledgment or assessment → obtain permitted instructor review → record source completion.

**Controls.** Curriculum, date, instructor, reminders. **Evidence.** Exact training/policy version and accepted result. **Boundary.** Acknowledgment, attendance, assessment and accepted completion are distinct.

<a id="roadmap-recipe-gen-09"></a>

##### GEN-09 — Credential or document renewal  \|  Phase 34

**Start and process.** An approved source expiry condition becomes due. Notify eligible participant → request replacement → review currentness → record accepted successor.

**Controls.** Lead time, owner, requirements, renewal reminders. **Evidence.** Current source requirement and replacement evidence. **Boundary.** Expiry cannot cause arbitrary access/financial changes outside source policy.

<a id="roadmap-recipe-gen-10"></a>

##### GEN-10 — Opportunity registration and waitlist  \|  Phase 37

**Start and process.** The event owner accepts a registration or waitlist occurrence. Collect entry requirements → request source capacity check/reservation → confirm or waitlist → send permitted next steps.

**Controls.** Intake questions, response deadline, role routing. **Evidence.** Registration/capacity outcome and participant tasks. **Boundary.** Event service owns atomic capacity and payment classification.

<a id="roadmap-recipe-gen-11"></a>

##### GEN-11 — Trip readiness and changes  \|  Phase 37

**Start and process.** An approved participant joins a trip or an event change is accepted. Collect required documents/training → observe source payment readiness → review departure checklist → notify source-approved changes → request financial handling separately.

**Controls.** Checklists, team roles, deadlines, approved messages. **Evidence.** Per-participant evidence and authorized readiness decision. **Boundary.** Participant payments and donations remain distinct; Studio cannot infer payment or refunds.

<a id="roadmap-recipe-gen-12"></a>

##### GEN-12 — Post-event follow-up  \|  Phase 37

**Start and process.** The event owner records completion. Request attendance confirmation → collect debrief/survey → assign follow-up → route future invitation only if eligible.

**Controls.** Questions, cadence, follow-up owner. **Evidence.** Source attendance, debrief, next-action decision. **Boundary.** Attendance alone does not authorize marketing or certify training.

<a id="roadmap-recipe-gen-13"></a>

##### GEN-13 — Shared-inbox routing  \|  Phase 34

**Start and process.** Support Hub accepts a conversation. Match permitted routing facts → assign eligible team/owner or explicit unassigned queue → create source-owned response task.

**Controls.** Topic/language/source-safe CRM conditions, team, fallback. **Evidence.** Source conversation and assignment outcome. **Boundary.** No second inbox, broad sender auto-create, or assignment-derived access.

<a id="roadmap-recipe-gen-14"></a>

##### GEN-14 — Support acknowledgment  \|  Phase 34

**Start and process.** Support Hub accepts an acknowledgment-eligible conversation. Check source loop/auto-submitted guards → request approved acknowledgment → retain conversation task independently.

**Controls.** Business-hours wording, response expectation, approved sender. **Evidence.** Source eligibility, communication intent and thread correlation. **Boundary.** No autoresponder loops; not every inbound message deserves acknowledgment.

<a id="roadmap-recipe-gen-15"></a>

##### GEN-15 — Support response-target escalation  \|  Phase 34

**Start and process.** Support owner records an approaching or breached target. Observe source business clock → remind eligible owner → escalate through approved team route → stop when source target is satisfied.

**Controls.** Native target policy, calendar, eligible escalation roles. **Evidence.** Source target occurrence and response result. **Boundary.** Studio must not create a parallel SLA clock or suppress required source attention.

<a id="roadmap-recipe-gen-16"></a>

##### GEN-16 — Waiting-on-requester and reopen  \|  Phase 34

**Start and process.** Support owner accepts waiting/snooze/reply transition. Apply source-supported follow-up → wait on source reply → preserve or reassign eligible owner → resume source work.

**Controls.** Follow-up interval within policy, reminder maximum, eligible owner. **Evidence.** Source conversation transition and accepted follow-up. **Boundary.** A reply or snooze is not resolution; old queued reminders must be fenced.

<a id="roadmap-recipe-gen-17"></a>

##### GEN-17 — Department handoff  \|  Phase 34

**Start and process.** Support Hub accepts a transfer request. Prepare permitted internal context → assign receiving team → request acknowledgment → retain accountability until accepted.

**Controls.** Receiving role, checklist, response time. **Evidence.** Source transfer and receiving-owner acknowledgment. **Boundary.** Internal notes cannot be delivered as customer messages; no automatic broad record sharing.

<a id="roadmap-recipe-gen-18"></a>

##### GEN-18 — Sensitive conversation routing  \|  Phase 38

**Start and process.** Support classification owner identifies restricted subject matter. Route into source-authorized restricted area → issue only approved safe acknowledgment → remove ordinary queue exposure as source permits.

**Controls.** Authorized destination and nonrevealing message. **Evidence.** Opaque accepted restricted handoff. **Boundary.** Care content and existence cannot leak to ordinary support staff or reports.

<a id="roadmap-recipe-gen-19"></a>

##### GEN-19 — Donor/account service request  \|  Phase 34

**Start and process.** Support source opens a verified service case. Collect minimum source facts → request authorized financial/identity operation → wait for exact source result → communicate permitted outcome.

**Controls.** Intake questions, owner and approved messages. **Evidence.** Verified request and independently authorized source outcome. **Boundary.** No generic task-approved refund, recurring restart, or identity change.

<a id="roadmap-recipe-gen-20"></a>

##### GEN-20 — Quarantine and inbound/delivery recovery  \|  Phase 34

**Start and process.** Support source records quarantine or delivery failure. Assign safe review → inspect source-allowed evidence → request source recovery → confirm conversation/communication outcome.

**Controls.** Responsible team, urgency within source rules. **Evidence.** Source review/recovery and separately recorded message state. **Boundary.** No silent message deletion, internal-note leak, raw provider replay or loop bypass.

<a id="phase-44-don-donor-services-and-development"></a>

#### DON — Donor services and development

<a id="roadmap-recipe-don-01"></a>

##### DON-01 — First organization gift welcome  \|  Phase 35

**Start and process.** Contribution owner certifies a first qualifying organizational gift. Confirm source first-gift fact → resolve donor-care owner → request purpose-approved welcome → create personal follow-up → record confirmed outcomes.

**Controls.** Welcome publication, follow-up owner/due date, approved channels. **Evidence.** Qualifying contribution and first-gift fact, source communication, task result. **Boundary.** No inference from incomplete import history; official receipt remains independent.

<a id="roadmap-recipe-don-02"></a>

##### DON-02 — First designation gift introduction  \|  Phase 35

**Start and process.** Contribution owner certifies first qualifying gift to a designation. Resolve designation-safe recipient context → coordinate ministry introduction and staff/missionary task → suppress duplicate purposes.

**Controls.** Designation content, responsible role, cadence. **Evidence.** Source designation-first fact and permitted recipient projection. **Boundary.** Anonymous identity and restricted-worker aliases remain protected.

<a id="roadmap-recipe-don-03"></a>

##### DON-03 — Threshold or special-gift follow-up  \|  Phase 35

**Start and process.** A qualifying source contribution meets explicit criteria. Compare same-currency approved amount basis → create personal acknowledgment task → notify eligible relationship owner.

**Controls.** Currency threshold, inclusive boundary, owner, timing. **Evidence.** Source amount/currency and task acknowledgment. **Boundary.** No cross-currency scalar or inferred donor intent.

<a id="roadmap-recipe-don-04"></a>

##### DON-04 — Anonymous-gift awareness  \|  Phase 35

**Start and process.** A qualifying contribution is source-labeled anonymous. Request privacy-safe summary → notify authorized staff/missionary according to purpose → optionally create non-identifying task.

**Controls.** Whether to notify, grouping, authorized recipients. **Evidence.** Source anonymity projection and requested summary. **Boundary.** Donor identity cannot appear in public/missionary payload, task, URL, or trace.

<a id="roadmap-recipe-don-05"></a>

##### DON-05 — Tribute acknowledgment  \|  Phase 35

**Start and process.** Recognition owner records tribute audience eligibility. Review required recipient information → prepare purpose-specific acknowledgment → request permitted delivery → resolve missing details.

**Controls.** Wording, source-permitted recipients, delivery preference. **Evidence.** Recognition source and delivery result. **Boundary.** Legal donor and tribute recipient are different; no inappropriate tax receipt.

<a id="roadmap-recipe-don-06"></a>

##### DON-06 — DAF and soft-credit stewardship  \|  Phase 35

**Start and process.** Recognition source records a DAF/soft-credit occurrence. Resolve relationship follow-up audience → assign thank-you/cultivation work → request approved nonreceipt message.

**Controls.** Owner, wording, cadence. **Evidence.** Source recognition refs and recorded outreach. **Boundary.** Recognition does not rewrite legal donor or receipt eligibility.

<a id="roadmap-recipe-don-07"></a>

##### DON-07 — Matching-gift follow-up  \|  Phase 35

**Start and process.** The owner opens an eligible matching-gift case. Collect employer/source details → request evidence → review submission → track source accepted match outcome.

**Controls.** Questions, owner, follow-up dates. **Evidence.** Match evidence, reviewed case result, posted contribution links if any. **Boundary.** No match money before source posted contribution or source-qualified completion.

<a id="roadmap-recipe-don-08"></a>

##### DON-08 — Refund or correction communication  \|  Phase 35

**Start and process.** The financial owner confirms a correction/refund outcome. Observe exact outcome → request authorized donor communication → assign any remaining service work.

**Controls.** Approved content and owner. **Evidence.** Confirmed source outcome and communication purpose identity. **Boundary.** No workflow-controlled refund, legal-donor change, or invented completion.

<a id="roadmap-recipe-don-09"></a>

##### DON-09 — New recurring commitment orientation  \|  Phase 35

**Start and process.** Recurring owner records a new authorized commitment. Observe source terms and communication eligibility → create approved staff follow-up → request orientation only if not already owned by source.

**Controls.** Content within source contract, owner, optional follow-up. **Evidence.** Source commitment transition and separate received-gift facts. **Boundary.** No duplicate state notice, payment retry, or claim that scheduled means received.

<a id="roadmap-recipe-don-10"></a>

##### DON-10 — Recurring occurrence attention  \|  Phase 35

**Start and process.** Recurring owner records a named health/occurrence transition. Observe source recovery policy → assign eligible donor-service task → request only permitted supplementary follow-up → await source result.

**Controls.** Staff routing and permitted escalation. **Evidence.** Exact occurrence transition, source eligibility and recovery result. **Boundary.** No second dunning/retry sequence; pause is not failure; absent gift is not debt.

<a id="roadmap-recipe-don-11"></a>

##### DON-11 — Recurring pause or end follow-up  \|  Phase 35

**Start and process.** Recurring owner accepts pause/skip/cancel/resume/end transition. Route appropriate staff awareness → coordinate requested assistance → observe source-authorized successor where relevant.

**Controls.** Optional relationship follow-up and approved wording. **Evidence.** Exact source lifecycle transition. **Boundary.** Canceled authority cannot be resurrected; restart needs fresh authorization.

<a id="roadmap-recipe-don-12"></a>

##### DON-12 — Fixed-pledge milestones  \|  Phase 35

**Start and process.** Pledge owner records explicit reminder enrollment or fulfillment milestone. Observe eligible milestone → send only source-allowed reminder/acknowledgment → create staff task if needed.

**Controls.** Narrow or disable source reminder policy, owner, approved wording. **Evidence.** Pledge fulfillment/eligibility evidence. **Boundary.** Reminder program remains opt-in/off by default and within source maximum.

<a id="roadmap-recipe-don-13"></a>

##### DON-13 — Contribution inactivity review  \|  Phase 35

**Start and process.** Source semantic report identifies a completeness-qualified inactivity cohort. Freeze permitted cohort → exclude contact restrictions → assign human relationship review → request consented outreach where appropriate.

**Controls.** Lookback scope, review owner, cooldown, eligible message. **Evidence.** Report basis/coverage, consent decision, review outcome. **Boundary.** No person-level lapsed label or override of recurring source health.

<a id="roadmap-recipe-don-14"></a>

##### DON-14 — Cultivation stages and next actions  \|  Phase 34

**Start and process.** Development owner accepts enrollment or stage transition. Assign next action → require relevant information → review stage aging → escalate missing next action.

**Controls.** Allowed stage preset, task cadence, owner. **Evidence.** Source stage transition and next task. **Boundary.** Stage is not access, legal donor, commitment, or money truth.

<a id="roadmap-recipe-don-15"></a>

##### DON-15 — Ask/proposal and appeal coordination  \|  Phase 34

**Start and process.** Development owner opens a proposal or approved appeal cohort. Prepare supporting facts → request required human review → assign outreach → observe source responses → schedule stewardship.

**Controls.** Source-permitted reviewer routing, audience filters, cadence. **Evidence.** Exact proposal/appeal approval and source response. **Boundary.** Never-ask/contact restrictions and explicit currency/entity remain binding.

<a id="roadmap-recipe-don-16"></a>

##### DON-16 — Church relationship and milestone review  \|  Phase 34

**Start and process.** A church partnership or permitted anniversary review becomes due. Prepare source-safe relationship brief → assign personal contact → record next action and agreed responsibilities.

**Controls.** Milestone choice, contact owner, questions, cadence. **Evidence.** Reviewed relationship facts and next-action record. **Boundary.** Relationship milestones do not supply permission or marketing consent.

<a id="phase-44-mob-mobilization-and-onboarding"></a>

#### MOB — Mobilization and onboarding

<a id="roadmap-recipe-mob-01"></a>

##### MOB-01 — Inquiry through discovery  \|  Phase 41

**Start and process.** Mobilization intake accepts an inquiry. Assign coordinator → acknowledge receipt → schedule discovery → record proceed/follow-up/refer/close outcome.

**Controls.** Program routes, coordinator, questions, response targets. **Evidence.** Discovery submission and source disposition. **Boundary.** No automatic missionary membership from inquiry.

<a id="roadmap-recipe-mob-02"></a>

##### MOB-02 — Application submission and review  \|  Phase 41

**Start and process.** A new application engagement is accepted. Invite participant → collect versioned form → allow save/resume → request corrections → review complete submission.

**Controls.** Fields, conditional sections, coordinator, reminders. **Evidence.** Exact form and accepted submission versions. **Boundary.** Answers map only to permitted application/CRM fields; no overwrite of history.

<a id="roadmap-recipe-mob-03"></a>

##### MOB-03 — Reference collection  \|  Phase 41

**Start and process.** Application owner issues reference requirements. Collect nominees → qualify category and contact purpose → send scoped requests → collect questionnaires → review required category/quantity evidence.

**Controls.** Questionnaires, required categories/count, reminder cadence. **Evidence.** Accepted reference evidence per required category. **Boundary.** Required church reference cannot be replaced by arbitrary any-two; restricted data stays sealed.

<a id="roadmap-recipe-mob-04"></a>

##### MOB-04 — Interviews and assessments  \|  Phase 41

**Start and process.** The approved plan requires interviews. Assign eligible interviewers → schedule tasks → conduct interviews → submit assessments → request authorized review.

**Controls.** Interview kinds, parallel/sequence order, forms, deadlines. **Evidence.** Interview occurrence and accepted assessment versions. **Boundary.** Calendar end is not completed interview; assignment grants no extra record access.

<a id="roadmap-recipe-mob-05"></a>

##### MOB-05 — Screening coordination  \|  Phase 41

**Start and process.** Application source issues a screening requirement. Obtain required source consent → request certified/manual screening → route result to authorized reviewer → observe source clearance.

**Controls.** Eligible reviewer, required evidence, reminders. **Evidence.** Source screening determination without private contents in workflow state. **Boundary.** No AI approval, public clinical upload, or unqualified screening provider.

<a id="roadmap-recipe-mob-06"></a>

##### MOB-06 — Decision and conditional acceptance  \|  Phase 41

**Start and process.** Application is ready for authorized decision. Prepare evidence bundle → request required human approval → record acceptance/conditions/deferral/decline → release permitted communication.

**Controls.** Decision roles within policy, condition tasks, wording. **Evidence.** Exact decision and approved conditions. **Boundary.** No task checkbox, elapsed timer, or broad admin bypass of decision authority.

<a id="roadmap-recipe-mob-07"></a>

##### MOB-07 — Appointment agreements  \|  Phase 41

**Start and process.** The source records accepted appointment terms. Prepare versioned documents → request required signers → verify qualified signature evidence → resolve document replacement.

**Controls.** Document sets, signer routing, dates. **Evidence.** Current agreement and signer evidence. **Boundary.** Acceptance is not signing; superseded document signatures do not qualify.

<a id="roadmap-recipe-mob-08"></a>

##### MOB-08 — Account and operational setup  \|  Phase 41

**Start and process.** A source-approved appointment permits onboarding. Request identity/account setup → route finance/operations tasks → confirm source outcomes → hand off to receiving owner.

**Controls.** Checklist, departments, due dates. **Evidence.** Identity/operations source outcomes and accepted handoff. **Boundary.** No direct account grants, Field Account creation, financial succession, or permission from template role.

<a id="roadmap-recipe-mob-09"></a>

##### MOB-09 — Training and orientation  \|  Phase 41

**Start and process.** Appointment source assigns preparation requirements. Assign required courses/resources → collect submissions → request instructor assessment → review permitted prior learning.

**Controls.** Curriculum, prerequisites, instructor, deadlines. **Evidence.** Accepted completion or independently authorized waiver evidence. **Boundary.** Attendance/acknowledgment is not certified completion; nonwaivable rules remain.

<a id="roadmap-recipe-mob-10"></a>

##### MOB-10 — Final readiness and handoff  \|  Phase 41

**Start and process.** Required onboarding lanes have source-qualified evidence. Recheck current required evidence → obtain final authorized readiness decision → request receiving-team acknowledgment → publish participant-safe milestone.

**Controls.** Optional checklist and receiving role. **Evidence.** Final readiness approval and receiving-owner acknowledgment. **Boundary.** Accepted, onboarded, ready, and deployed remain distinct source milestones.

<a id="roadmap-recipe-mob-11"></a>

##### MOB-11 — Hold, withdrawal, and reapplication  \|  Phase 41

**Start and process.** An authorized participant/staff lifecycle request is accepted. Apply source disposition → cancel optional future requests safely → handle clocks → revoke limited links → open new application for reapplication.

**Controls.** Pauseable reminder settings, owner, approved messages. **Evidence.** Source lifecycle outcome and explicit new application lineage. **Boundary.** Completed history and grants remain source-owned; withdrawal is not delete.

<a id="roadmap-recipe-mob-12"></a>

##### MOB-12 — Individual plan amendment  \|  Phase 41

**Start and process.** Authorized staff requests case-specific variation. Prepare impact preflight → validate added/removed requirements → obtain required review → apply new plan revision → notify permitted participants.

**Controls.** Eligible extra steps, owner, deadline, permitted waivers. **Evidence.** Approved amendment digest, evidence coverage and future-work changes. **Boundary.** No retroactive erase, duplicate sends, or weakening of nonwaivable requirements.

<a id="phase-44-fin-protected-finance-coordination"></a>

#### FIN — Protected finance coordination

<a id="roadmap-recipe-fin-01"></a>

##### FIN-01 — Offline gift/batch exception follow-up  \|  Phase 34

**Start and process.** Contribution owner records a batch or gift exception. Assign finance reviewer → request missing source information → open native correction → verify source resolution.

**Controls.** Owner, reminders, exception urgency within policy. **Evidence.** Exact exception and accepted source correction. **Boundary.** No raw money edits, fake donor identity, or automatic posting.

<a id="roadmap-recipe-fin-02"></a>

##### FIN-02 — Receipt/statement delivery remediation  \|  Phase 34

**Start and process.** Document/communication owner records a failure. Inspect source eligibility/current artifact → request compatible source retry or destination correction → verify separate outcomes.

**Controls.** Review owner, allowed delivery preferences. **Evidence.** Current artifact plus source delivery/exception result. **Boundary.** No regenerated legal facts or duplicated official document.

<a id="roadmap-recipe-fin-03"></a>

##### FIN-03 — Year-end statement operations coordination  \|  Phase 34

**Start and process.** Finance creates an authorized statement-run request. Prepare native source preflight → assign review tasks → use source release → coordinate paper work and exceptions.

**Controls.** Native profile settings, eligible recipients, staffing checklist. **Evidence.** Statement source run, item-authoritative outcomes, separate fulfillment. **Boundary.** Studio cannot freeze population, change totals, or own the source run schedule.

<a id="roadmap-recipe-fin-04"></a>

##### FIN-04 — Accounting handoff review  \|  Phase 34

**Start and process.** Accounting owner marks a source package ready for review. Assign authorized review → inspect exact native preflight → request permitted release → observe source/provider outcome.

**Controls.** Checklist, authorized owner, notifications. **Evidence.** Source-approved release and independently recorded delivery outcome. **Boundary.** No arbitrary journal, provider replay, or Studio-created release.

<a id="roadmap-recipe-fin-05"></a>

##### FIN-05 — Reconciliation investigation  \|  Phase 34

**Start and process.** Accounting owner records a discrepancy. Gather allowed references → assign investigator → coordinate source correction → verify source-accepted disposition.

**Controls.** Owner, evidence request, escalation. **Evidence.** Source discrepancy and accepted resolution. **Boundary.** Task complete is not bank/QBO/Xero reconciliation.

<a id="roadmap-recipe-fin-06"></a>

##### FIN-06 — Support cycle close preparation  \|  Phase 34

**Start and process.** Field Account owner creates a cycle review occurrence. Notify eligible finance role → gather source exceptions → request native review/close → observe source-completed close.

**Controls.** Native cadence and reviewer notification. **Evidence.** Finance-closed source cycle and exact through-date. **Boundary.** No close from checklist, no recomputed balance, no silent currency conversion.

<a id="roadmap-recipe-fin-07"></a>

##### FIN-07 — Support plan review  \|  Phase 34

**Start and process.** Source opens a Support Plan version for review. Collect supporting data → request authorized review → publish approved source projection if permitted → alert coaching only through allowed bridge.

**Controls.** Reviewer within contract, checklist, dates. **Evidence.** Source-approved Plan Version and projection consent. **Boundary.** Fundraising goal, balance, compensation, and plan remain separate.

<a id="roadmap-recipe-fin-08"></a>

##### FIN-08 — Expense evidence follow-up  \|  Phase 34

**Start and process.** Expense owner records missing or insufficient evidence. Mirror source follow-up task → request exact evidence through owner → observe claimant response and source review → stop on resolved source requirement.

**Controls.** Notification routing and bounded reminder policy only. **Evidence.** Exact claim/evidence version and source resolution decision. **Boundary.** No choosing protected reviewer, auto approval, claimant fact authoring, or custom financial case state.

<a id="roadmap-recipe-fin-09"></a>

##### FIN-09 — Expense review coordination  \|  Phase 34

**Start and process.** Expense owner accepts a submitted claim needing review. Open source finite review route → notify assigned eligible reviewer → coordinate missing information → observe source decision.

**Controls.** Native source review settings and permitted notifications. **Evidence.** Source assignment snapshot and claim-level decision. **Boundary.** Self/AI/timeout/automatic approval prohibited; report task does not approve every claim.

<a id="roadmap-recipe-fin-10"></a>

##### FIN-10 — Advance and reimbursement follow-up  \|  Phase 34

**Start and process.** Source records an advance/obligation requiring attention. Gather source-qualified supporting evidence → route authorized finance task → observe settlement/payment coverage from source.

**Controls.** Responsible team and follow-up wording. **Evidence.** Source obligation, settlement and external-payment evidence. **Boundary.** No payment execution, assumed settlement, or treating missed amount as collectible debt.

<a id="roadmap-recipe-fin-11"></a>

##### FIN-11 — Uncertain external handoff investigation  \|  Phase 34

**Start and process.** Finance provider owner records outcome unknown. Quarantine duplicate execution → assign investigator → request source readback → resolve confirmed/non-applied/unknown coverage.

**Controls.** Operational owner and alert urgency. **Evidence.** Exact source/provider reconciliation outcome. **Boundary.** No blind retry, provider switching, assumed paid, or timer release of reserved coverage.

<a id="roadmap-recipe-fin-12"></a>

##### FIN-12 — Worker/designation retirement coordination  \|  Phase 34

**Start and process.** Source accepts a governed exit or retirement case. Review source succession requirements → assign donor service and records tasks → request independently authorized recurring/financial changes → verify source outcomes.

**Controls.** Checklist, owners, communication routing. **Evidence.** Source exit manifest and independently accepted downstream decisions. **Boundary.** No automatic money redirection, canceled-donor authorization revival, hold release, or record disposal.

<a id="phase-44-mpd-missionary-work-and-coaching"></a>

#### MPD — Missionary work and coaching

<a id="roadmap-recipe-mpd-01"></a>

##### MPD-01 — Gift-driven missionary thank-you  \|  Phase 35

**Start and process.** Contribution source qualifies missionary follow-up. Obtain permitted supporter projection → create one source-purpose thank-you task → coordinate with organization donor care → record interaction.

**Controls.** Eligible gift situations, due date, grouping preference. **Evidence.** Source gift purpose and shared interaction/task outcome. **Boundary.** No anonymous-donor disclosure or duplicated organization message.

<a id="roadmap-recipe-mpd-02"></a>

##### MPD-02 — Supporter outreach sequence  \|  Phase 34

**Start and process.** Development source enrolls a permitted prospect. Set next action → request appointment follow-up → record source outcome → stop on terminal/suppressed state.

**Controls.** Organization-approved preset, cadence, questions. **Evidence.** Source stage and next-action record. **Boundary.** Never-ask/current consent and relationship visibility remain binding.

<a id="roadmap-recipe-mpd-03"></a>

##### MPD-03 — Referral follow-up  \|  Phase 34

**Start and process.** A permitted supporter referral is recorded. Verify purpose and relationship scope → assign contact task → log outcome → expire unpursued referral by source rule.

**Controls.** Cadence, owner, approved questions. **Evidence.** Referral source, eligibility and interaction outcome. **Boundary.** Referral does not grant broad CRM enumeration or newsletter consent.

<a id="roadmap-recipe-mpd-04"></a>

##### MPD-04 — Coaching check-in  \|  Phase 34

**Start and process.** A tenant-approved coaching occurrence becomes due. Request short qualitative/activity report → share approved redacted projection with coach → obtain feedback → record next agreed action.

**Controls.** Cadence, questions, eligible coach, agreed targets. **Evidence.** Check-in version, coaching feedback and next action. **Boundary.** Coach access is explicit and redacted; no raw supporter/care detail.

<a id="roadmap-recipe-mpd-05"></a>

##### MPD-05 — Goal/plan compare and review  \|  Phase 34

**Start and process.** Approved source goal or plan version changes. Show authorized comparison → request human goal review → optionally create new source Goal Version with provenance.

**Controls.** Review timing and coaching owner. **Evidence.** Explicit source goal decision and provenance. **Boundary.** No live synchronization of finance Plan, goal, commitment, balance or compensation.

<a id="roadmap-recipe-mpd-06"></a>

##### MPD-06 — Named support attention review  \|  Phase 35

**Start and process.** Source recurring/commitment owner issues a qualified attention event. Create permitted relationship task → review exact occurrence context → request approved follow-up only → await source result.

**Controls.** Task owner and permitted cadence. **Evidence.** Source occurrence/health transition and task outcome. **Boundary.** No person-level lapsed label, inferred debt or second dunning sequence.

<a id="roadmap-recipe-mpd-07"></a>

##### MPD-07 — Personal appeal milestone and close  \|  Phase 34

**Start and process.** Development source records an appeal milestone/end. Review authorized supporter response → assign acknowledgments → collect brief outcome review → set next steps.

**Controls.** Milestones, task cadence, allowed audience. **Evidence.** Source appeal outcome and acknowledged follow-up. **Boundary.** Currency/entity basis and source permission remain fixed.

<a id="roadmap-recipe-mpd-08"></a>

##### MPD-08 — Ministry Update drafting reminder  \|  Phase 34

**Start and process.** An approved communication cadence becomes due. Create draft task → provide permitted prompt/template → route submitted update to communications workflow → stop redundant reminders.

**Controls.** Cadence, author, optional editor. **Evidence.** Submitted update revision and handoff. **Boundary.** No automatic publication or raw donor email; communication remains source-owned.

<a id="phase-44-com-communications-and-public-content"></a>

#### COM — Communications and public content

<a id="roadmap-recipe-com-01"></a>

##### COM-01 — Ministry Update editorial publication  \|  Phase 34

**Start and process.** Content owner accepts an update revision for review. Assign review → collect corrections → obtain source approval for exact revision → request publication → observe published state → request approved distribution.

**Controls.** Editors, review steps, schedule within source contract. **Evidence.** Exact revision, source approval, publication and distinct distribution outcome. **Boundary.** Approval for an old revision cannot publish changed content; restricted visibility persists.

<a id="roadmap-recipe-com-02"></a>

##### COM-02 — Missionary/project page change  \|  Phase 34

**Start and process.** CMS owner records a permitted page proposal. Review content → request authorized amendments → perform safety review if required → request source publication.

**Controls.** Reviewer routing, checklist, approved wording. **Evidence.** Exact CMS revision and source publication decision. **Boundary.** Public identity and operational identity remain distinct; no publication bypass.

<a id="roadmap-recipe-com-03"></a>

##### COM-03 — New page preparation  \|  Phase 34

**Start and process.** Source records a ministry/project that may have a public page. Assign author → collect permitted biography/media → review draft → request source publication when allowed.

**Controls.** Template, author/reviewer, checklist. **Evidence.** Approved source/public identity mapping and published revision. **Boundary.** Source existence is not permission to disclose a restricted worker.

<a id="roadmap-recipe-com-04"></a>

##### COM-04 — Restricted-worker content review  \|  Phase 34

**Start and process.** Source content requires restricted-ministry review. Route only authorized reviewers → inspect source-safe content → record exact safety decision → request permitted publication.

**Controls.** Eligible reviewers and additional nonwaiving tasks. **Evidence.** Source safety determination and exact publication evidence. **Boundary.** Mandatory safety checks cannot be removed; content and run existence are restricted.

<a id="roadmap-recipe-com-05"></a>

##### COM-05 — Translation and locale publication  \|  Phase 34

**Start and process.** Content owner requests a locale version. Assign translator → collect versioned translation → obtain locale review → request native locale publication.

**Controls.** Locales, translator/reviewer, dates. **Evidence.** Exact translation and locale publication. **Boundary.** One locale publication does not imply all locales approved or alter identity/currency.

<a id="roadmap-recipe-com-06"></a>

##### COM-06 — Seasonal scheduling and stale-content review  \|  Phase 34

**Start and process.** CMS schedule/review owner creates an occurrence. Prepare or review content → record authorized decision → request source schedule/retirement → verify native result.

**Controls.** Native dates, content classes, review owner. **Evidence.** Source schedule/review decision and publication state. **Boundary.** Studio cannot duplicate CMS scheduling or create another published flag.

<a id="roadmap-recipe-com-07"></a>

##### COM-07 — Comment/media moderation  \|  Phase 34

**Start and process.** Source moderation queue records a flag. Assign eligible reviewer → inspect safe source content → request permitted moderation outcome → notify where appropriate.

**Controls.** Routing, target response interval, approved notices. **Evidence.** Source moderation outcome and separate notification. **Boundary.** Malware/privacy protections remain mandatory; no AI-only harmful-content decision.

<a id="roadmap-recipe-com-08"></a>

##### COM-08 — Page retirement and safe redirection  \|  Phase 34

**Start and process.** Source lifecycle approves page retirement review. Review public wording and financial destination → request native archive/redirect only after owner approval → verify public-safe outcome.

**Controls.** Reviewer, checklist, approved explanation. **Evidence.** Source retirement/redirect decision and financial approval reference if required. **Boundary.** No automatic designation or money redirection from content changes.

<a id="roadmap-recipe-com-09"></a>

##### COM-09 — Newsletter and welcome communications  \|  Phase 34

**Start and process.** Source audience owner records valid topic enrollment or approved send request. Prepare governed publication → review permitted audience → request source-owned schedule/send → observe suppression and delivery → route replies to Support Hub.

**Controls.** Content, eligible audience filters, schedule through owner. **Evidence.** Source audience eligibility, exact publication, delivery and reply refs. **Boundary.** Donation alone is not subscription consent; unsubscribes remain effective.

<a id="roadmap-recipe-com-10"></a>

##### COM-10 — Message/sender failure remediation  \|  Phase 34

**Start and process.** Message/connection owner records missing publication, bounce or sender failure. Route responsible editor/operator → open source correction → verify readiness → reconcile affected unsent intent.

**Controls.** Owner, urgency, approved checklist. **Evidence.** Source readiness/suppression outcome and exact intent disposition. **Boundary.** No unsafe fallback sender, template, duplicate send or newsletter resubscribe.

<a id="phase-44-care-member-care-and-confidential-lifecycle"></a>

#### CARE — Member care and confidential lifecycle

<a id="roadmap-recipe-care-01"></a>

##### CARE-01 — Confidential intake  \|  Phase 38

**Start and process.** Member-care owner accepts a request into sealed scope. Assign source-qualified carer → acknowledge through safe purpose channel → collect source intake acknowledgment → observe accepted care handoff.

**Controls.** Eligible care role, safe acknowledgment, follow-up interval. **Evidence.** Opaque care-intake acceptance and authorized handoff. **Boundary.** No ordinary-admin existence signal or clinical facts in workflow state.

<a id="roadmap-recipe-care-02"></a>

##### CARE-02 — Routine care check-in  \|  Phase 38

**Start and process.** Care owner creates an approved check-in occurrence. Notify eligible participant safely → record source-owned response → assign permitted care follow-up → confirm receiving carer.

**Controls.** Cadence, source-approved questions, carer. **Evidence.** Source check-in and follow-up acknowledgment. **Boundary.** Care notes are not CRM notes; routing does not grant access.

<a id="roadmap-recipe-care-03"></a>

##### CARE-03 — Care-team handoff  \|  Phase 38

**Start and process.** Care owner authorizes a case assignment change. Prepare source-limited handoff → request receiving-carer acknowledgment → revoke superseded access through owner → verify handoff.

**Controls.** Eligible receiving role, checklist, timing. **Evidence.** Source access/assignment versions and acknowledged handoff. **Boundary.** No transitive access from team membership or broad staff hierarchy.

<a id="roadmap-recipe-care-04"></a>

##### CARE-04 — Home assignment or sabbatical preparation  \|  Phase 38

**Start and process.** Authorized source lifecycle opens a transition. Coordinate ordinary logistics separately from sealed care work → request permitted check-ins → confirm receiving responsibility.

**Controls.** Checklists, dates, ordinary/clinical separation. **Evidence.** Separately scoped source transition and care acknowledgments. **Boundary.** No release of care information to logistics or finance.

<a id="roadmap-recipe-care-05"></a>

##### CARE-05 — Return-to-field preparation  \|  Phase 38

**Start and process.** Source opens a return readiness review. Collect permitted preparation → request source-qualified reviews → confirm authorized readiness and handoff.

**Controls.** Checklist, eligible roles, schedule. **Evidence.** Source readiness decision and receiving-owner acknowledgment. **Boundary.** No automated medical fitness decision, inferred clearance, or unauthorized disclosure.

<a id="roadmap-recipe-care-06"></a>

##### CARE-06 — Crisis coordination  \|  Phase 38

**Start and process.** Authorized care/crisis source declares an incident. Activate source-approved contact tasks → track acknowledgment → escalate through approved tree → link emergency access only through source break-glass.

**Controls.** Authorized response roles, acknowledgment timing, approved contact tree. **Evidence.** Source incident actions and acknowledgments, not inferred proof of life. **Boundary.** Workflow cannot grant emergency access, prove safety, or replace emergency services; alternate communication is required.

<a id="roadmap-recipe-care-07"></a>

##### CARE-07 — After-action and emergency-access review  \|  Phase 38

**Start and process.** Crisis/access source records review-required occurrence. Assign independent eligible reviewer → inspect source-permitted records → record follow-up → request source revocation/correction as authorized.

**Controls.** Review owner and schedule. **Evidence.** Source post-incident review and access outcome. **Boundary.** Sensitive-read history is itself restricted; task completion is not access revocation.

<a id="roadmap-recipe-care-08"></a>

##### CARE-08 — Confidential offboarding and privacy request  \|  Phase 38

**Start and process.** Care/records owner accepts departure or verified privacy case. Route verified purpose → request owner-filtered records/review → coordinate respectful handoff → observe source-authorized outcome.

**Controls.** Safe communication and authorized task timing. **Evidence.** Source-authorized response/disposition and handoff evidence. **Boundary.** No export-as-erasure, blanket archive, hold release, or clinical record disposal timer.

Slice new work into independently verifiable user-visible behavior and bind it to current owner contracts. Do not let a package-wide completion edge reverse a valid phase dependency.

<a id="phase-44-web-studio-journeys"></a>

#### Web Studio journeys

| **Journey** | **Observable handoff or boundary** |
| --- | --- |
| WF01 — Create a visual-first Site and first Page | Staff creates a useful page with no GitHub account; second Site never inherits another Site’s draft or brand accidentally. |
| WF02 — Compose and edit a Page visually | Canvas and non-canvas operations produce identical canonical documents; text changed after developer redesign still updates the correct rendered field. |
| WF03 — Use bounded advanced layouts | A long translated Split layout collapses without content loss or visual/DOM reordering; non-drag moves work on touch and keyboard. |
| WF04 — Select and replace qualified media | Two placements of one image retain different alt/crop metadata; revoked rights defeat a stale candidate and cached positive qualification. |
| WF05 — Reuse a section without hidden global edits | Editing a shared quote does not silently publish ten drafts; independent local copy no longer tracks shared edits. |
| WF06 — Create or update an exact-locale version | A Thai Page and English source can diverge safely; copying produces private work and cannot change locale enablement. |
| WF07 — Change Site appearance or a supported component variant | Content-only editor cannot change a whole Site brand; Page variant changes do not affect sibling Sites. |
| WF08 — Review and publish content or composition | Reviewer publishes the selected headline while later private draft remains private; failed compile keeps the previous safe generation. |
| WF09 — Schedule exact content publication or removal | Execute/cancel races yield one permitted effect; an appointment after provider dedupe expiry still cannot publish twice. |
| WF10 — Recover a save conflict or restore a draft | Two same-user tabs cannot race silently; restore retains published output and meaningful history. |
| WF11 — Connect a ministry-controlled custom repository | A repo administrator without Asym permission cannot connect another Tenant; an Asym admin without repository authority cannot seize source. |
| WF12 — Develop a custom presentation through normal tools | Fresh clone works without Core private source, production credentials, Asym IDE or model account; staff editing still works after redesign. |
| WF13 — Build and independently admit custom presentation | Malicious postinstall cannot read the source-fetch token; weakened repository tests cannot pass independent forbidden-import/binding checks. |
| WF14 — Review and activate a custom Site design | One locale failure prevents partial design activation; deployment skew never silently serves another package. |
| WF15 — Evolve a semantic type or migrate presentation settings | Old and new readers/writers are tested both ways; production content is never replaced by the developer database. |
| WF16 — Replace a developer, reconnect or disconnect source | Agency replacement during staff editing preserves content and live safe website; duplicate events cannot reconnect old source. |
| WF17 — Inspect an exact private preview | Preview cannot submit real donations/forms, access another Tenant or fall through to Live when a route is absent. |
| WF18 — Hand over the website and use approved platform capabilities | A staff member independently completes representative tasks; restricted worker identity never enters custom code props, fixtures, public search or logs. |

<a id="phase-44-fixed-web-studio-automation"></a>

#### Fixed Web Studio automation

AU01 and AU02 remain editor/request behavior. The other entries use fixed source-owned work and the shared durable substrate where required. None is an optional tenant workflow or a new publication/schedule authority.

| **Native behavior** | **Owner** | **Effect and recovery** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| AU01 — Coalesced editorial autosave | D12 Editorial operations; WF02, WF03, WF10. | Validate structure, reprove lease/revision/permission; commit content and receipt together. No ordinary notifications, Git builds or public effects. Recovery: Serialize/coalesce; same command/key on lost acknowledgement; stop successor saves for stale/revoked/unknown outcome. |
| AU02 — Acknowledged working-preview refresh | Preview operations; WF02, WF08, WF17. | Refresh only the saved preview version; later local edits labelled unsaved. Never publish. Recovery: Deduplicate/coalesce obsolete requests; a failed renderer does not roll back the saved draft. |
| AU03 — Source discovery and reconciliation | Integration owner; WF11, WF12, WF16. | Persist event before dispatch; discover eligible revision and request a bounded capture/build. No source writes or automatic activation. Recovery: Authenticated webhook receipt dedupe plus business identity; shared bounded reconcile for missed deliveries. |
| AU04 — Clean build and qualification | Presentation build/admission owner; WF12, WF13. | Claim product work; run isolated code; record exact artifact/evidence; hand to independent admission. Never grant the worker serving-head writes. Recovery: Transient infrastructure retries bounded; deterministic code/schema failures stop with diagnostics; reconcile unknown external task before retry. |
| AU05 — Fixed preview/candidate preparation | D25/D1 and D10 owner; WF08, WF14, WF17. | Briefly snapshot, compile outside locks, reprove and seal complete candidate or none. Later drafts not silently included. Recovery: Current expected-head races obey owning reprepare rules; unknown receipt looked up. |
| AU06 — Scheduled publication executor | D13 with shared Inngest execution; WF09. | Read organization authorization and current safety; execute the same D1 command, preserving unrelated work. Recovery: Shared ledger/claim and overdue recovery; no-before time; stale event no-op; semantic conflict needs attention. |
| AU07 — Public projection convergence | Cache, search and media delivery owners; WF08, WF14. | Dispatch identifier-only intents; make derived systems reflect committed public generation. No new favorable authority. Recovery: Version-aware replay ignores older favorable results; own proof/read policy handles current adverse safety. |
| AU08 — Adverse public safety containment | Phase 10/media/package safety owner; WF04, WF08, WF14, WF18. | Suppress through authoritative read/egress boundary immediately; invalidate dependent previews/candidates and converge caches. Recovery: Idempotent adverse replay; prioritize over routine build jobs. No wait for optional webhook or search index. |
| AU09 — Compatibility and impact refresh | Catalog/presentation owner; WF05, WF07, WF13, WF15. | Derive affected Page count/details allowed by permission; detect unsupported bindings. No automatic content mutation. Recovery: Bounded incremental rebuild; incomplete projection labelled unknown, never unused. |
| AU10 — Repository lifecycle handling | Integration owner; WF11, WF16. | Rename updates labels; ownership/control changes require re-verification; disconnect fences new source work. Preserve admitted safe artifacts. Recovery: Reconcile ambiguous provider outcome; outage is not proof of deletion. Older events cannot reactivate access. |
| AU11 — Dispatch and unknown-outcome recovery | Existing shared dispatch + effect owner; WF08, WF09, WF13, WF14. | Repair delivery or query original outcome under current registered purpose. Do not invent success from queue status. Recovery: Bounded backoff and claim fencing; semantic failure routed to owner; provider dedupe window not sufficient. |
| AU12 — Preview expiry and retained-artifact maintenance | Preview and custody owners; WF14, WF16, WF17. | Expire grants/compute; derive retained use evidence; purge only separately authorized eligible disposable bytes. Recovery: Idempotent operations with unknown deletion reconciliation; missing references block disposal. |
