<a id="ws-chapter-7"></a>

### 7. Build plan, acceptance, rollout, and operations


<a id="ws-h-delivery-waves"></a>

#### Delivery waves

> **Integration note:** These original specification waves describe the whole workflow program. Phase 34 CORE uses its roadmap-defined non-mobilization tracers and closes independently; gift-pack, full application, event and care proof closes with its owning phase. WS-26 is the combined rollup, not a backward dependency. See [IG-01](#ig-01) and [IG-03](#ig-03).


Waves describe sequencing within this specification, not new roadmap phase numbers or authorization to skip dependencies.

| Wave | Deliverable | Exit evidence |
|---|---|---|
| W0 — authority and substrate | Binding map, registry contracts, domain-ready matrix, additive schema design, threat model, source event correctness | OpenSpec review, Core Guardian review, source owners agree exact allowed commands |
| W1 — executable foundation | AST/compiler, state transitions, event intake, semantic operations, wait handshake, two real vertical slices | Gift-follow-up and inquiry flows work using real source services, not mocked effects |
| W2 — authoring and participation | Guided editor, canvas/outline, forms, external tasks, My Work/My Journey, simulation, publication | Accessible staff and external-participant end-to-end tests |
| W3 — long processes and amendments | Full mobilization, parallel work, training/documents, plan revisions, version migration | Evidence-currentness, late-event, concurrency, cancellation, and upgrade drills |
| W4 — cross-product packs | Support, development, coaching, publishing, events, document and operational recipes | Each pack passes owning-source capability/readiness tests |
| W5 — protected and restricted lanes | Finance coordination and member-care orchestration | Independent approval invariants, zero existence leaks, provider/data-handling qualification |
| W6 — pilot and rollout | Per-tenant activation, operational tooling, documentation, cost/load results | Representative-tenant usability tests, rollback and restore evidence, no critical findings |

No wave is complete because the templates are visible. No member-care scope activates before sealed projections and provider qualification. No finance scope activates by exposing the prototype correction/replay actions.

<a id="ws-h-repository-placement"></a>

#### Repository placement

Proposed shared contract module can start under the existing workflow package boundary rather than immediately introducing a new workspace. Prefer `packages/api/src/workflows/studio/` for business services, a pure isomorphic contract/compiler module in the established shared package topology, `packages/database` for browser-safe query hooks/projections, and `packages/ui` for shared primitives. Mission Control owns editor composition; participant routes use their app's scoped projection. Read nearest `AGENTS.md`, current manifests, installed Next documentation, and tests before implementing each subtree [R1].

The supplied folder `openspec/changes/add-workflow-studio/` is a proposed change. Merge it into an existing covering active change when appropriate rather than creating contradictory authorities. Do not run `openspec update` or archive unfinished work [R2]. The specification supplies no production migration and applies none.

<a id="ws-h-required-tdd-suites"></a>

#### Required TDD suites

Compiler: malformed AST, type mismatches, node identity, predicate truth tables, unknown history, overlap, unselected branches, dominator analysis, subflow recursion, workload budgets, classification propagation, retired bindings, default-off posture.

State-machine/property tests: accepted events cannot produce duplicate effects; selected joins advance at most once; past decisions remain immutable; cancellation fences stale work; unrelated branches survive partial failure; publication changes do not change active plans. Generate shuffled events, duplicate events, lease expiries, source corrections, and concurrent edits.

Database: composite tenant isolation, source FKs, RLS and privileged-path negative tests, CAS, unique enrollment/effects, claim fencing, outbox atomicity, lower-sequence late commit, concurrent consumers, retention and restore tombstones. Do not substitute in-memory tests for database races.

Adapter: source-owned evidence, communications, assignments, permissions, signatures and webhooks, provider ambiguity, retry window expiry, source retirement, invalidation events, and safe source-specific result mapping. Each action has both a simulation implementation and a real integration test; simulation cannot call production transport.

UI/Playwright: build a simple rule; create a parallel application; preview roles; recover a missing owner; edit one active plan; ensure no duplicate message; complete an external form on mobile; handle poor connectivity; keyboard-only authoring; assistive-technology review; return-to-task focus; server-side field exclusion.

Security: cross-tenant IDs, staff-to-care enumeration, unauthorized derived conditions, source-access revocation between preflight and dispatch, malicious form/email text, unsafe attachment/reference URLs, CSRF, token scanners, guessed task IDs, secret leakage in traces and error reports, destructive imported definitions.

<a id="ws-h-proposed-performance-and-reliability-targets"></a>

#### Proposed performance and reliability targets

Targets below are acceptance requirements to measure under documented infrastructure and load, not current production performance claims. Record CPU, memory, database size, hosted plan, dataset, region, browser, network profile, and observed results in evidence.

| Measurement | Initial target |
|---|---|
| Accepted source events | No loss in fault-injection suite; every accepted event has a durable receipt/outbox identity |
| Duplicate business effects | Zero in replay/race/recovery fixtures; uncertain outcomes never silently retried |
| Interactive editor | 250-node expanded fixture remains usable; p95 interaction feedback under 100 ms on agreed reference laptop |
| Participant task mutation | p95 authoritative acceptance under 1 s excluding file upload/provider execution on agreed baseline |
| Normal event-to-visible-task lag | p95 under 10 s, p99 under 60 s at certified load; source receipt time is reported |
| Recovery scan | Finds due stalled work within 5 min of healthy execution recovery; outage independent alert has tested coverage |
| Workload test | At least 100 tenant fixtures, 100k dormant engagements, 10k due operations, and a 10x burst tenant without cross-tenant leakage or accepted-work loss |
| Accessibility | WCAG 2.2 AA target; automated checks plus manual keyboard and screen-reader acceptance |

Thresholds may be revised through an evidence-backed spec amendment before launch. Do not hide a failing test by changing the target after measurement without recorded approval.

<a id="ws-h-operational-runbooks"></a>

#### Operational runbooks

**Missing work:** identify source event and binding generation; inspect durable receipt, publication readiness, enrollment key, run health, and source task. Repair the smallest missing handoff. Do not re-fire the whole donor lifecycle.

**Uncertain email/provider result:** inspect prepared intent and exact source request identity; query the authorized provider evidence path; confirm or retain `outcome_unknown`; resend only when the contract proves safe or an authorized new business communication is explicitly created.

**Revoked grant or departed staff:** suspend affected new optional operations; reassign work through authorized source services; review grant ownership; do not grant blanket admin access. Preserve irreversible completed facts.

**Bad template publication:** disable new enrollment for that binding; inspect impact cohort; continue unaffected old versions; prepare per-run amendments or discontinuation. Do not alter immutable history or remove required source operations.

**Provider outage:** continue accepted source writes and queue work; distinguish essential versus optional capacity; surface operational health. Reopen gradually with current permission and suppression checks, not a catch-up flood.

**Database restore:** keep outward effects and grant changes disabled; reconcile prior operations and revocations; preserve disposal tombstones; verify no duplicate or resurrected effect before enabling tenant batches.

<a id="ws-h-metrics"></a>

#### Metrics

Use authorized, source-labeled metrics: run age, waiting-on-staff/applicant/external-source time, missing owners, due work, unknown outcomes, confirmed source handoffs, duplicate attempts prevented, eligible notifications suppressed, late timer wake, amended plans, abandoned drafts, and publication errors. Avoid a universal progress percentage. Care-related aggregates remain protected. Financial metrics use their owning reporting definitions; Studio never sums incomparable currencies or sources.

<a id="ws-h-go-no-go-gates"></a>

#### Go / no-go gates

Do not release with any unresolved cross-tenant or restricted-existence leak, unauthorized source command, duplicate external effect, lost accepted event, blind ambiguous retry, unsafe payment/expense approval, invalid evidence completion, or irreversible history rewrite. A missing provider integration cannot be disguised by a mock green node.

Before full release, choose representative design partners: small agency, larger multi-region agency, sending church/network, and restricted-ministry organization. Staff must create a real rule without a developer, amend one applicant, and recover a stalled process; participants must complete their part on a phone. Record findings, not assumed satisfaction.

<a id="ws-h-repository-verification-to-run-during-implementation"></a>

#### Repository verification to run during implementation

Use the locally pinned CLI and current scripts: `bun run openspec -- validate add-workflow-studio --strict`, `bun run openspec:validate`, `bun run lint`, `bun run typecheck`, `bun run test:unit`, relevant Playwright/a11y suites, `bun run format:check`, `bun run verify:workspace-contract`, `bun run check`, and `bun run ci:preflight`. Inspect current commands before use. This package's own validation is not a claim these repository checks ran.

<a id="ws-h-remaining-external-decisions-with-safe-defaults"></a>

#### Remaining external decisions, with safe defaults

| Gate | Accountable owner | Evidence needed | Safe behavior before resolution |
|---|---|---|---|
| Exact Inngest deployment/plan and data handling | Platform/security | Current contract, retention/access/residency, load and failover tests | Synthetic development only for unqualified restricted lanes |
| Exact e-sign provider/capability | Document/domain owner | Signature/evidence semantics, webhook and ambiguity tests, tenant authorization | Manual reviewed evidence where policy permits; automated signing dark |
| Screening provider/capability | Mobilization/security | Exact lawful purpose, access/retention, source evidence tests | Authorized manual screening; no fake provider result |
| Current source seams and DB names | Owning implementation teams | Repo inventory and compatibility tests | Do not introduce parallel owner or unsafe migration |
| Domain retention schedules | Data/records owners | Approved purpose-specific schedules and holds | No arbitrary Studio disposal timer |
| Licensed layout dependency/version | Frontend/security | Exact package/license provenance, browser performance | Manual layout/outline remain fully usable |
| Tenant operational thresholds | Tenant publisher/domain owner | Activation preview with concrete dates/currency/recipients | Suggested defaults remain inert until accepted |

<a id="ws-chapter-8"></a>

### 8. Core workflow and automation catalog


This catalog specifies **96 recipes in eight role-oriented packs**. They are normative product recipes, not a claim of 96 implemented integrations. The reference blueprints exercise representative recipes; source adapters and tenant bindings are separate activation prerequisites.

All recipes inherit the language, authorization, evidence, scheduling, idempotency, communication, revision, and recovery contracts. Suggested timing is configurable within source policy and never overrides it. Every optional starter installs disabled. A protected operation is a link/request to its source owner, not a generic programmable approval. [R3, R4]

<a id="ws-h-catalog-index"></a>

#### Catalog index

| Pack | Intended user | Recipes |
|---|---|---|
| ADM — Administration and operations | Tenant administrator or operations lead | 10 |
| GEN — Small-team and common operations | Small-team staff member wearing several hats | 20 |
| DON — Donor services and development | Donor services and development staff | 16 |
| MOB — Mobilization and complete onboarding | Mobilization staff, interviewers, and trainers | 12 |
| FIN — Finance and protected operations | Finance staff | 12 |
| MPD — Missionary work and coaching | Missionaries and coaches | 8 |
| COM — Communications and public content | Communications and website staff | 10 |
| CARE — Member care and confidential lifecycle | Member-care staff | 8 |

Required source capabilities: identity, crm, tasks, workflow-runtime. These symbolic capability names must map to the existing owners; they are not existing repository APIs.

<a id="ws-h-adm-01-staff-onboarding"></a>

##### ADM-01 — Staff onboarding

**Subject:** `staff_onboarding`. **Envelope:** editable workflow. **Default:** disabled.

**Starts when:** An authorized staff onboarding request is accepted.

**Process:** Confirm intended responsibilities → collect policy acknowledgments → request source-authorized access → assign orientation → verify receiving manager handoff.

**Tenant controls:** Checklist, eligible role slots, orientation schedule, approved message.

**Required evidence / completion:** Policy acknowledgments, role-request refs, orientation completion, handoff acceptance.

**Protected boundary:** Access grants remain identity-owned and require independent current authorization.

**Timing:** Source-owned timing wins; otherwise propose three business days, at most two optional outward reminders, and internal escalation. Tenant must approve concrete dates.

**Recipients and visibility:** Current authorized responsible role; participant-specific projection only where source permits. No raw source records in workflow or email.

**Recovery:** Missing owner -> eligible source queue; unknown facts/outcomes -> block/reconcile; completed source history remains immutable.

**Tests:** `T-ADM-01-01` proves the intended source-backed outcome; `T-ADM-01-02` changes an allowed parameter and proves the protected boundary still holds; `T-ADM-01-03` replays and races completion with cancellation to prove one outcome without duplicate effects.

<a id="ws-chapter-9"></a>

### 9. Reference definitions and implementation binding contracts


The package includes **16 structured reference definitions** under `blueprints/`, a dialect JSON Schema, a machine-readable recipe catalog, and a source-contract register. These are build specifications and fixtures, not already installed tenant automations. All definitions are disabled, use synthetic semantic bindings instead of real tenant records, and reject historical enrollment by default.

Blueprints deliberately exercise the same DSL across simple automations and human processes. BP-04 spans application submission, parallel references/interviews/screening, decision routes, conditional requirements, and BP-05's post-acceptance agreements, training, operational setup, final readiness, and receiving handoff. “Onboarded” is not “deployed.” BP-06 coordinates expense evidence without approving claims. BP-09 keeps care metadata within a sealed purpose. BP-10 routes a Support Hub conversation without creating a separate inbox.

<a id="ws-h-blueprint-index"></a>

#### Blueprint index

| Definition | Recipe | What it proves in the eventual implementation |
|---|---|---|
| BP-01 | GEN-01 | Initial inquiry and accountable response |
| BP-02 | DON-01 | First-gift coordinated stewardship |
| BP-03 | ADM-01 | Staff onboarding with source-owned access |
| BP-04 | MOB-02 | Application through fully completed onboarding |
| BP-05 | MOB-08 | Post-acceptance onboarding through handoff |
| BP-06 | FIN-08 | Expense-evidence follow-up without approval authority |
| BP-07 | MPD-04 | Coaching check-in with redacted views |
| BP-08 | COM-01 | Ministry Update review and publication |
| BP-09 | CARE-01 | Sealed member-care intake |
| BP-10 | GEN-13 | Support conversation routing and response |
| BP-11 | GEN-06 | Private document request and review |
| BP-12 | GEN-10 | Registration and source-owned capacity |
| BP-13 | DON-10 | Recurring occurrence service follow-up |
| BP-14 | ADM-06 | Permitted custom-record review |
| BP-15 | DON-03 | Explicit currency/minor-unit threshold with tenant-reviewed parameters |
| BP-16 | GEN-09 | Durable wait on source-accepted renewal evidence |

<a id="ws-h-binding-completion-checklist"></a>

#### Binding completion checklist

For every contract in `contracts/source-contract-register.json`, the owning domain must provide a real versioned adapter, runtime and compile-time input/output schemas, source permission checks, allowed audience projection, event mapping, exact success/decline/unknown outcome meaning, permanent effect identity where applicable, source conflict/cancellation behavior, privacy-safe diagnostic result, and no-side-effect simulation fixture.

The current artifacts intentionally do not pretend these symbolic names already exist in Core. The target code must adapt existing services first. A newly invented `expenses.approve` implementation is not an acceptable substitute for the source-owned follow-up contract. A missing certified private-byte service cannot be replaced with a public upload bucket. A source event must be emitted from the authoritative accepted command, not inferred from an arbitrary table update.

A bound subflow invokes a separate child engagement at an exact published version and returns a source-approved outcome to its parent. Its terminal node ends only the child engagement. Parent and child record linked scope, causation, cancellation, and completion. No child gets more data or capabilities than the intersection of its own grant and the parent's permitted delegation. Reusing an already-completed child requires exact source/evidence equivalence; a new invocation cannot silently count an unrelated old completion.

<a id="ws-h-reference-fixture-limits"></a>

#### Reference fixture limits

The blueprints omit real message bodies and sensitive values by design. Tenant setup resolves the safe source publications, permitted forms, exact role qualifiers/fallbacks, calendar policy, and scope. Structural schema validation does not verify deployed source availability, tenant permissions, provider behavior, database races, or production performance. The included verification report lists only the checks actually executed while assembling this package.


<a id="ws-h-reference-semantics-requiring-source-qualification"></a>

#### Reference semantics requiring source qualification

BP-12 keeps a waitlisted registration active and waiting until the event owner records a final disposition. Capacity reservation, offer, participant acceptance, offer expiry and cancellation are native event-domain operations. Studio neither allocates seats from a count nor treats an elapsed deadline as approval. Source uncertainty keeps the wait open; named final non-admission outcomes use a separate branch. A held unknown disposition requires review, not silent restart.

BP-04's declined/withdrawn/deferred routes terminate with the exact process disposition. A later return uses the held-disposition/reapplication contract in the language specification. Source completion can also withdraw/cancel a run globally, including while it is waiting in a subflow; cancellation must fence pending work and reconcile already-started effects.

Required capability names are proposed readiness labels, not existing feature flags or permission grants. The register includes triggers as well as facts/actions and keeps every purpose for reused contracts; a contract certified for ordinary inquiry use is not thereby certified for care use.


<a id="ws-h-form-reference-fixtures"></a>

#### Form reference fixtures

Four inert form examples (`form-blueprints/FORM-01.json` through `FORM-04.json`) exercise inquiry capture, application, confidential reference, and coaching check-in. These are starting field sets, not a prescribed theological screening instrument or complete personnel/clinical questionnaire. Tenants bind permitted fields, wording and requirements through the source owner. No health or counseling question is placed in an ordinary application fixture.

The form schema defines versioned pages, field types, source-command mappings, conditional visibility, partial save, and immutable accepted submission snapshots. It is not a second CRM schema. In FORM-03, a private reply-email question appears only when the reference requests confidential follow-up. Its visible required status is enforced server-side; hidden values are excluded from accepted submissions and effects, with source-retention rules controlling any existing drafts/history. False, missing, and stale facts remain distinguishable.

Mappings are proposed owner-command and field contracts, never raw SQL paths. Displayed field classification can only be raised by tenant configuration; the source floor wins. Render and submission authorization is rechecked for every field. Version-dependent accepted answers do not change when a draft form is edited. Conditional visibility is not an access control. Form endpoints require purpose-bound access, rate limits, anti-CSRF where cookies apply, and semantic duplicate-submission checks. Private file requests use the separate evidence service rather than embedding file bytes here.

<a id="ws-chapter-11"></a>

### 11. Acceptance scenario catalog


These are **tests to implement and execute**, not claims of test execution. The package verification report separately lists the static checks performed for these artifacts.

<a id="ws-h-cross-cutting-adversarial-scenarios"></a>

#### Cross-cutting adversarial scenarios

<a id="ws-h-ws-at-001-tenant-isolation"></a>

##### WS-AT-001 — Tenant isolation

**Given:** Tenant A owns a run.

**When:** Tenant B submits its run ID.

**Then:** Return non-enumerating denial; no state or timing-sensitive detail is disclosed.

<a id="ws-h-ws-at-002-publish-is-not-source-authority"></a>

##### WS-AT-002 — Publish is not source authority

**Given:** Publisher can edit workflow but cannot authorize expense decisions.

**When:** They add a direct approval action.

**Then:** Catalog/compiler and source service reject it.

<a id="ws-h-ws-at-003-revocation-after-preflight"></a>

##### WS-AT-003 — Revocation after preflight

**Given:** A valid publication preflight exists.

**When:** Publisher/source grant is revoked before confirmation.

**Then:** Confirmation fails without publication or side effect.

<a id="ws-h-ws-at-004-runtime-revocation"></a>

##### WS-AT-004 — Runtime revocation

**Given:** An operation is queued.

**When:** Source capability is revoked before dispatch.

**Then:** Operation blocks with safe reason and no forbidden call.

<a id="ws-h-ws-at-005-confidential-existence"></a>

##### WS-AT-005 — Confidential existence

**Given:** A sealed care run exists.

**When:** An ordinary admin filters, searches, exports, or counts workflows.

**Then:** No name, membership, count, or audit existence signal escapes.

<a id="ws-h-ws-at-006-derived-sensitive-fact"></a>

##### WS-AT-006 — Derived sensitive fact

**Given:** A care-only fact would determine an outward message.

**When:** A user attempts a condition over it.

**Then:** Compilation blocks unauthorized use and derived information flow.

<a id="ws-h-ws-at-007-cross-entity-request"></a>

##### WS-AT-007 — Cross-entity request

**Given:** A valid tenant contains two Legal Entities.

**When:** Workflow attempts incompatible source action across entity scopes.

**Then:** Owning service rejects; no implicit entity/currency coercion.

<a id="ws-h-ws-at-008-assignment-is-not-permission"></a>

##### WS-AT-008 — Assignment is not permission

**Given:** An interviewer is assigned.

**When:** They request unrelated care or donor data.

**Then:** Server projection denies unrelated data.

<a id="ws-h-ws-at-009-unknown-is-not-false"></a>

##### WS-AT-009 — Unknown is not false

**Given:** A reference clearance fact is not yet known.

**When:** Choose-one evaluates its branches.

**Then:** Run waits/blocks; it does not decline or take fallback.

<a id="ws-h-ws-at-010-overlapping-cases"></a>

##### WS-AT-010 — Overlapping cases

**Given:** Two cases are true.

**When:** Choose-one evaluates.

**Then:** Ambiguity blocks; no first-row winner.

<a id="ws-h-ws-at-011-true-plus-unknown"></a>

##### WS-AT-011 — True plus unknown

**Given:** One exclusive case is true and another unknown.

**When:** Choose-one evaluates.

**Then:** Exclusivity is not proved; no action starts.

<a id="ws-h-ws-at-012-required-join-category"></a>

##### WS-AT-012 — Required join category

**Given:** Two nonchurch references arrive; church reference is mandatory.

**When:** Quorum count is numerically satisfied.

**Then:** Requirement remains unsatisfied until required source category qualifies.

<a id="ws-h-ws-at-013-unselected-branch"></a>

##### WS-AT-013 — Unselected branch

**Given:** A guarded branch is known false.

**When:** Parallel join waits on selected work.

**Then:** False branch is not awaited and does not count as evidence.

<a id="ws-h-ws-at-014-empty-parallel-selection"></a>

##### WS-AT-014 — Empty parallel selection

**Given:** No branch activates and onEmpty is block.

**When:** Node is evaluated.

**Then:** It blocks rather than silently succeeding.

<a id="ws-h-ws-at-015-unavailable-branch-output"></a>

##### WS-AT-015 — Unavailable branch output

**Given:** A downstream input depends on an optional branch without export handling.

**When:** Template is published.

**Then:** Compiler rejects the dataflow reference.

<a id="ws-h-ws-at-016-no-coercion"></a>

##### WS-AT-016 — No coercion

**Given:** String "false" or "100" appears where Boolean/integer is required.

**When:** Predicate evaluation is attempted.

**Then:** Validation fails; no JavaScript truthiness.

<a id="ws-h-ws-at-017-currency-safe-threshold"></a>

##### WS-AT-017 — Currency-safe threshold

**Given:** USD threshold meets a THB fact.

**When:** Condition is evaluated.

**Then:** Incompatible money context cannot pass through numerical comparison.

<a id="ws-h-ws-at-018-incomplete-first-gift-history"></a>

##### WS-AT-018 — Incomplete first-gift history

**Given:** An import omits earlier gifts.

**When:** First-gift recipe evaluates.

**Then:** Source fact remains unknown; no fabricated welcome eligibility.

<a id="ws-h-ws-at-019-duplicate-event"></a>

##### WS-AT-019 — Duplicate event

**Given:** An accepted event has already created an effect.

**When:** Same event arrives after provider dedupe expires.

**Then:** Permanent source semantic identity prevents duplicate effect.

<a id="ws-h-ws-at-020-out-of-order-commit"></a>

##### WS-AT-020 — Out-of-order commit

**Given:** Higher-numbered outbox row commits first.

**When:** Consumer advances while lower row is uncommitted.

**Then:** Lower accepted row is eventually processed; cursor protocol does not skip it.

<a id="ws-h-ws-at-021-historical-import"></a>

##### WS-AT-021 — Historical import

**Given:** Legacy gifts are imported.

**When:** Workflow binding is enabled.

**Then:** Historical effects remain dark absent explicit reviewed backfill.

<a id="ws-h-ws-at-022-wrong-source"></a>

##### WS-AT-022 — Wrong source

**Given:** A raw payment provider callback exists.

**When:** A user attempts to treat it as posted contribution.

**Then:** No donation stewardship enrollment until owning source qualifies facts.

<a id="ws-h-ws-at-023-cross-workflow-loop"></a>

##### WS-AT-023 — Cross-workflow loop

**Given:** Workflow A triggers B and B triggers A.

**When:** Causation exceeds allowed budget.

**Then:** Chain is quarantined visibly without unbounded execution.

<a id="ws-h-ws-at-024-wrong-correlation"></a>

##### WS-AT-024 — Wrong correlation

**Given:** An old signature for a superseded agreement arrives.

**When:** Wait consumer processes it.

**Then:** It cannot satisfy current agreement requirement.

<a id="ws-h-ws-at-025-completion-before-wait"></a>

##### WS-AT-025 — Completion before wait

**Given:** Reference completion commits before wait row.

**When:** Wait registers later.

**Then:** Immediate source recheck discovers accepted completion.

<a id="ws-h-ws-at-026-completion-after-wait"></a>

##### WS-AT-026 — Completion after wait

**Given:** Wait row commits first.

**When:** Completion event arrives.

**Then:** Consumer locates exact wait and advances it.

<a id="ws-h-ws-at-027-lost-wake"></a>

##### WS-AT-027 — Lost wake

**Given:** Source evidence and wait exist.

**When:** Immediate dispatch and event wake are lost.

**Then:** Indexed reconciliation eventually advances from source facts.

<a id="ws-h-ws-at-028-two-simultaneous-completions"></a>

##### WS-AT-028 — Two simultaneous completions

**Given:** Two required branches finish.

**When:** Both workers try to advance join.

**Then:** One accepted transition; both evidence records preserved.

<a id="ws-h-ws-at-029-cancel-while-queued"></a>

##### WS-AT-029 — Cancel while queued

**Given:** Reminder is prepared but not dispatched.

**When:** Run cancellation commits first.

**Then:** Epoch/fence check suppresses stale reminder.

<a id="ws-h-ws-at-030-cancel-after-accepted-send"></a>

##### WS-AT-030 — Cancel after accepted send

**Given:** Provider accepted the message.

**When:** User cancels the run.

**Then:** UI records irreversible send and cancels only remaining safe work.

<a id="ws-h-ws-at-031-expired-lease-after-dispatch"></a>

##### WS-AT-031 — Expired lease after dispatch

**Given:** Worker may have sent externally then disappears.

**When:** Lease expires.

**Then:** Operation becomes uncertain; no blind second send.

<a id="ws-h-ws-at-032-concurrent-draft-editors"></a>

##### WS-AT-032 — Concurrent draft editors

**Given:** Two users edit revision 4.

**When:** Second writes after first creates revision 5.

**Then:** Conflict is visible; no silent overwrite.

<a id="ws-h-ws-at-033-new-template-publication"></a>

##### WS-AT-033 — New template publication

**Given:** Applicant runs on version 1.

**When:** Version 2 is published.

**Then:** Applicant remains on version 1.

<a id="ws-h-ws-at-034-individual-extra-interview"></a>

##### WS-AT-034 — Individual extra interview

**Given:** One applicant requires an added interview.

**When:** Authorized amendment is accepted.

**Then:** Only that run changes; completed evidence remains.

<a id="ws-h-ws-at-035-cosmetic-layout-edit"></a>

##### WS-AT-035 — Cosmetic layout edit

**Given:** Template graph is rearranged.

**When:** Layout is saved.

**Then:** Execution digest and business effects remain unchanged.

<a id="ws-h-ws-at-036-retired-contract"></a>

##### WS-AT-036 — Retired contract

**Given:** A referenced form/action is retired.

**When:** An old draft attempts publication.

**Then:** Dependency check blocks or requires explicit compatible binding.

<a id="ws-h-ws-at-037-runtime-upgrade"></a>

##### WS-AT-037 — Runtime upgrade

**Given:** Old run uses action contract v1.

**When:** Deployment introduces incompatible v2.

**Then:** Old run executes supported v1 or is controlled-blocked for migration.

<a id="ws-h-ws-at-038-postcompletion-evidence-correction"></a>

##### WS-AT-038 — Postcompletion evidence correction

**Given:** Completed onboarding evidence is revoked by its owner.

**When:** Correction event arrives.

**Then:** Linked remediation is created; historical accepted decision is not rewritten.

<a id="ws-h-ws-at-039-business-day-timing"></a>

##### WS-AT-039 — Business-day timing

**Given:** Task due uses a holiday calendar.

**When:** Deadline crosses weekend/holiday.

**Then:** Proposed due time follows pinned business calendar.

<a id="ws-h-ws-at-040-dst-gap"></a>

##### WS-AT-040 — DST gap

**Given:** Local schedule targets a nonexistent clock time.

**When:** Timer is resolved.

**Then:** Next valid instant is used and resolution recorded.

<a id="ws-h-ws-at-041-pause-clocks"></a>

##### WS-AT-041 — Pause clocks

**Given:** Relative reminder and fixed document expiry coexist.

**When:** Run pauses.

**Then:** Relative remaining duration freezes; fixed expiry continues.

<a id="ws-h-ws-at-042-outage-catch-up"></a>

##### WS-AT-042 — Outage catch-up

**Given:** Many routine reminders become overdue.

**When:** Execution recovers.

**Then:** Policy coalesces safely; no catch-up message flood.

<a id="ws-h-ws-at-043-lost-provider-response"></a>

##### WS-AT-043 — Lost provider response

**Given:** Provider accepts message but response is lost.

**When:** Retry window expires.

**Then:** Reconcile or review; do not send a new blind copy.

<a id="ws-h-ws-at-044-shared-purpose"></a>

##### WS-AT-044 — Shared purpose

**Given:** Organization and missionary workflows request identical effect.

**When:** Both enqueue.

**Then:** Owning semantic key converges to one effect or reports incompatible payload conflict.

<a id="ws-h-ws-at-045-suppression-changed"></a>

##### WS-AT-045 — Suppression changed

**Given:** Optional message was prepared.

**When:** Recipient opts out before dispatch.

**Then:** Current source policy suppresses appropriate message; required security policy remains separate.

<a id="ws-h-ws-at-046-webhook-duplicate-order"></a>

##### WS-AT-046 — Webhook duplicate/order

**Given:** Delivery/bounce events repeat and arrive out of order.

**When:** Consumer updates source history.

**Then:** Deduped source facts retain correct meaning, not last-arrival overwrite.

<a id="ws-h-ws-at-047-reply-threading"></a>

##### WS-AT-047 — Reply threading

**Given:** Applicant replies to an approved workflow email.

**When:** Inbound source accepts it.

**Then:** Reply joins Support Hub/CRM context; no parallel workflow inbox.

<a id="ws-h-ws-at-048-trace-minimization"></a>

##### WS-AT-048 — Trace minimization

**Given:** Private record is needed inside action.

**When:** Action executes and errors.

**Then:** No raw values, signed URLs, bodies, or secrets appear in step state/logs.

<a id="ws-h-ws-at-049-protected-review"></a>

##### WS-AT-049 — Protected review

**Given:** Reviewer task receives a checkbox completion.

**When:** No source approval has been accepted.

**Then:** Financial/appointment evidence does not become approved.

<a id="ws-h-ws-at-050-external-scanner"></a>

##### WS-AT-050 — External scanner

**Given:** Email scanner follows a reference link.

**When:** GET occurs.

**Then:** No consume, sign, submit, grant, or irreversible action.

<a id="ws-h-ws-at-051-external-scope"></a>

##### WS-AT-051 — External scope

**Given:** Reference has a valid task session.

**When:** They request another task/applicant.

**Then:** Non-enumerating denial; no membership granted.

<a id="ws-h-ws-at-052-double-submission"></a>

##### WS-AT-052 — Double submission

**Given:** Mobile connection drops after accepted submit.

**When:** Participant retries same key.

**Then:** Original accepted submission is returned; no duplicate evidence.

<a id="ws-h-ws-at-053-quarantined-file"></a>

##### WS-AT-053 — Quarantined file

**Given:** Uploaded evidence is quarantined.

**When:** Review/evidence gate runs.

**Then:** File cannot qualify; safe replacement path exists.

<a id="ws-h-ws-at-054-old-revision-approval"></a>

##### WS-AT-054 — Old revision approval

**Given:** Content was approved then edited.

**When:** Publish operation runs.

**Then:** Exact-revision check blocks unreviewed content.

<a id="ws-h-ws-at-055-noisy-neighbor"></a>

##### WS-AT-055 — Noisy neighbor

**Given:** One tenant admits a 10x optional batch.

**When:** Other tenants have essential due work.

**Then:** Accepted work remains safe and agreed service targets are measured, not assumed.

<a id="ws-h-ws-at-056-orchestration-outage"></a>

##### WS-AT-056 — Orchestration outage

**Given:** Source writes succeed while Inngest is unavailable.

**When:** New work arrives.

**Then:** Source receipts/outbox persist and independent outage alert fires.

<a id="ws-h-ws-at-057-restore-safety"></a>

##### WS-AT-057 — Restore safety

**Given:** Database backup predates sent email and grant revocation.

**When:** System restores.

**Then:** Outbound remains disabled until effects/revocations/tombstones reconcile.

<a id="ws-h-ws-at-058-missing-provider"></a>

##### WS-AT-058 — Missing provider

**Given:** A blueprint references uncertified signing.

**When:** Tenant attempts activation.

**Then:** No mock success; automatic lane stays unavailable and valid manual path is labeled.

<a id="ws-h-ws-at-059-a11y-authoring"></a>

##### WS-AT-059 — A11y authoring

**Given:** Staff uses keyboard and screen reader.

**When:** They create, validate and publish a permitted simple rule.

**Then:** Complete outline path and focus/error feedback are usable.

<a id="ws-h-ws-at-060-poor-network"></a>

##### WS-AT-060 — Poor network

**Given:** Participant loses connection.

**When:** They edit and submit.

**Then:** Input is preserved safely; state remains pending until authoritative acceptance.

<a id="ws-h-ws-at-061-subflow-authority"></a>

##### WS-AT-061 — Subflow authority

**Given:** Parent has narrower permissions than reusable child.

**When:** Child invokes protected operation.

**Then:** Intersection applies; child cannot widen data or command authority.

<a id="ws-h-ws-at-062-subflow-cancellation"></a>

##### WS-AT-062 — Subflow cancellation

**Given:** Parent stops future work.

**When:** Child has queued and already-dispatched work.

**Then:** Cancellation propagates safely with irreversible work reported.

<a id="ws-h-ws-at-063-template-import"></a>

##### WS-AT-063 — Template import

**Given:** Inert portable blueprint contains foreign IDs or executable strings.

**When:** Tenant imports it.

**Then:** Validation rejects unsafe content; valid import remains disabled and requires rebinding.

<a id="ws-h-ws-at-064-retention-request"></a>

##### WS-AT-064 — Retention request

**Given:** A run contains source evidence references under hold.

**When:** Generic workflow timer expires.

**Then:** No hold release/disposal; owner governs lifecycle.

<a id="ws-h-recipe-acceptance"></a>

#### Recipe acceptance

Each of the 96 recipes has three stable acceptance IDs in the recipe catalog: source-backed completion, allowed customization with protected-boundary preservation, and replay/cancellation safety. Full machine-readable specifications are in `verification/acceptance-scenarios.json`. All 352 acceptance scenarios remain specified, not executed, until implemented in Core.

<a id="ws-chapter-12"></a>

### 12. Research and repository evidence


**Checked:** 2026-09-12. **Repository baseline:** `7abd2c11ffd4ed70c6775c4fd6f51c996e4350dd`. Sources support factual descriptions; proposed architecture, limits, defaults, UX and tests are design decisions, not vendor guarantees.

<a id="ws-h-reading-the-evidence"></a>

#### Reading the evidence

Current repo reality is determined by source/migrations/tests/runtime, not roadmap prose. This research read repository content through the connected GitHub tool; it did not run the application, inspect production tenant data, or execute repository CI. Official web documents were read directly. No unsupported competitor statistics are used.

<a id="ws-h-r1-core-repository-constitution"></a>

#### R1 — Core repository constitution
**Type:** Repository snapshot. **Retrieved/reviewed:** 2026-09-12.

**Source:** https://github.com/Asymmetric-al/core/blob/7abd2c11ffd4ed70c6775c4fd6f51c996e4350dd/AGENTS.md
Current package ownership, UI base-maia/Base UI requirement, source authority and verification rules.

<a id="ws-h-important-current-document-distinctions"></a>

#### Important current-document distinctions

The Inngest usage-limit page lists an event lookback allowance while the wait-for-event guide discusses a future lookback feature. This specification does not infer an available API or reliable retrospective delivery from either statement; the exact SDK capability must be tested. Durable source fact rechecks remain required regardless.

Workflow Kit documentation offers an installable package, while its current source README calls it a reference implementation. The recommendation follows the latter qualification: learn from the patterns, own the production dialect/compiler, and use current Inngest SDK guidance.

Provider plans, prices, region support, contractual data handling, and exact deployment characteristics were not verified for the user’s account. Their certification is an explicit release gate, not an assumption. No price or universal service-level promise is embedded in the spec.

The package includes a source of proposed behavior in OpenSpec format, not amendments already accepted into durable platform authority. In particular, authenticated applicant My Journey is an explicit proposed surface addition, not an existing authorization granted to applicants.

<a id="ws-h-13-proposed-openspec-change"></a>

### 13. Proposed OpenSpec change


<a id="ws-h-repository-relative-artifact-openspec-changes-add-workflow-studio-proposal-md"></a>

#### Repository-relative artifact: `openspec/changes/add-workflow-studio/proposal.md`

<a id="ws-h-change-add-a-shared-tenant-workflow-studio"></a>

### Change: Add a shared tenant Workflow Studio

<a id="ws-h-why"></a>

#### Why

Tenant staff need one place to author and operate supported workflows and automations across mobilization, donor stewardship, Support Hub, staff operations, content, training, and restricted care. The existing execution substrate and narrow contribution rules do not themselves provide complete tenant publication, evidence, participant, amendment, and recovery semantics.

<a id="ws-h-what-changes"></a>

#### What Changes

Add a Workflow Studio capability in Mission Control with a constrained versioned language, typed conditions, shared source action registry, immutable publications, explicit enrollment, role-bound tasks, durable evidence waits, scoped participant projections, per-run amendments, simulation, and operational recovery. Use React Flow as presentation and Inngest as shared execution; retain Core/Postgres/source domain ownership. Define an authenticated applicant/participant My Journey mode without creating broad missionary permissions.

Add role-oriented workflow recipes and source-certified adapter contracts. Phase 35 is a contribution pack on Phase 34, not a separate engine. Existing Support Hub/contribution rule data is adopted or migrated once; old and new evaluators cannot both own effects.

<a id="ws-h-non-goals-2"></a>

#### Non-goals

No tenant scripts, raw database writes, generic HTTP/credentials, iPaaS marketplace, replacement payment/accounting/identity/CMS/clinical systems, arbitrary financial approvals, child sponsorship, or Asym SaaS billing.

<a id="ws-h-impact"></a>

#### Impact

Affected capabilities: new `workflow-studio`; additive `platform-surfaces` participant requirement; existing `workflow-orchestration`, source permissions, communications and domain owner adapters are consumed without weakening their rules. Affected code areas are Mission Control, participant projections in existing apps, shared API/contracts/hooks/UI, additive database records, existing workflow runtime and source-owner adapters.

Full design: `docs/prds/workflow-studio/00-scope-and-decisions.md` through `11-research-and-repository-evidence.md`. Machine-readable dialect, recipes, bindings, example definitions and acceptance specifications accompany the change.

<a id="ws-h-compatibility-and-rollback"></a>

#### Compatibility and rollback

Preserve old deep links and manual source operations. Migrate rule ownership using shadow evaluation with effects disabled, compare outcomes, then atomically select one execution owner. Disable new optional enrollment to roll back; preserve accepted source facts, existing runs, compatible contract versions and durable outbox work. Never delete history or reverse external effects by editing a workflow.

<a id="ws-h-status"></a>

#### Status

Proposed, not implemented or archived. No migration, GitHub issue, deployment, provider activation, or source-authority change is claimed by this package. Verify against current active changes and source dependencies before incorporation. Validate using the repository-pinned CLI.

#### Repository-relative artifact: `openspec/changes/add-workflow-studio/design.md`

<a id="ws-h-design-workflow-studio"></a>

### Design: Workflow Studio

<a id="ws-h-context-and-chosen-architecture"></a>

#### Context and chosen architecture

Core's current workflow orchestration contract keeps product truth and business idempotency with source records and operates shared tenant-scoped execution infrastructure. The proposed product extends that foundation rather than creating another engine.

The canonical source is a typed structured AST. A pure compiler validates references, branch semantics, source readiness, authorization purposes, and workload bounds; the React Flow canvas and outline are views over that AST. A pure evaluator calculates next work. Short Postgres transactions record accepted transitions and source-bound operation requests. Bounded Inngest functions execute approved domain operations and wake the process from authoritative results.

Definitions, publications, enrollment bindings, engagement lifecycle, execution health, source task/evidence/communication status, and per-run revisions remain distinct. Protected financial, identity, records and publication operations remain source-owned. Participant views are purpose-specific projections, not full staff graphs with hidden fields.

<a id="ws-h-detailed-contracts"></a>

#### Detailed contracts

- Product and UX: `docs/prds/workflow-studio/01-product-and-experience.md`.
- Language/compiler: `docs/prds/workflow-studio/02-workflow-language.md` and `contracts/workflow.schema.json`.
- Runtime/races/recovery: `docs/prds/workflow-studio/03-runtime-and-recovery.md`.
- Data/API/registry: `docs/prds/workflow-studio/04-data-and-api-contracts.md`.
- Security/domains: `docs/prds/workflow-studio/05-security-and-domain-boundaries.md`.
- Build/operational gates: `docs/prds/workflow-studio/06-release-and-acceptance.md`.
- Recipes/reference bindings: `docs/prds/workflow-studio/07-core-workflow-catalog.md` and `08-blueprints-and-binding-contracts.md`.
- Backlog and acceptance: `09-implementation-backlog.md`, `10-acceptance-scenarios.md`, and machine-readable verification fixtures.
- Evidence and unresolved external qualification: `11-research-and-repository-evidence.md`.

These paths are repository-relative references. Preserve the existing spec-driven OpenSpec schema and repository instruction system; the workflow JSON dialect is a product data schema, not an OpenSpec configuration replacement.

<a id="ws-h-migration-and-implementation-constraints"></a>

#### Migration and implementation constraints

Read source and nearest AGENTS files before editing any subtree. Keep APIs thin in apps, domain work in packages/api, shared primitives in packages/ui, and exact base-maia/Base UI. Proposed table and route names are not permission to duplicate equivalent existing owners. Use additive migrations, one execution owner per rule, preserved semantic keys, protected source commands, and explicit contract compatibility.

<a id="ws-h-verification-and-rollback"></a>

#### Verification and rollback

TDD at the nearest stable seam, real database race tests, source adapter certification, secret and existence-leak tests, accessibility/participant tests, fault injection, load and cost measurement, and controlled pilot are required. A static blueprint validation is not a product release. Rollback disables optional new enrollment and preserves all source history and accepted work; uncertain external effects remain under reconciliation.

<a id="ws-h-repository-relative-artifact-openspec-changes-add-workflow-studio-specs-workflow-studio-spec-md"></a>

#### Repository-relative artifact: `openspec/changes/add-workflow-studio/specs/workflow-studio/spec.md`

<a id="ws-h-workflow-studio"></a>

### Workflow Studio

<a id="ws-h-added-requirements"></a>

#### ADDED Requirements

<a id="ws-h-requirement-one-shared-studio"></a>

##### Requirement: One Shared Studio
The system SHALL provide one Mission Control workflow authoring and operation capability with contextual module entry points. Simple and visual authoring MUST use one definition and execution vocabulary.

<a id="ws-h-scenario-ws-rq-001-supported-behavior"></a>

###### Scenario: WS-RQ-001 supported behavior
- GIVEN A staff member opens a Support Hub automation from module settings
- WHEN the automation is edited and published
- THEN the same definition and history appear in Workflow Studio; no second engine executes it

<a id="ws-h-requirement-source-authority"></a>

##### Requirement: Source Authority
The Studio MUST invoke only registered, source-authorized operations and MUST NOT manufacture financial, identity, clinical, signature, or publication truth.

<a id="ws-h-scenario-ws-rq-002-supported-behavior"></a>

###### Scenario: WS-RQ-002 supported behavior
- GIVEN A workflow task is checked complete without a source approval
- WHEN downstream work requests approved financial evidence
- THEN the required source decision remains unsatisfied and no protected effect occurs

<a id="ws-h-requirement-typed-conditional-logic"></a>

##### Requirement: Typed Conditional Logic
Predicates SHALL be typed and use explicit true, false and unknown results. Unauthorized fields MUST be blocked, not treated as absent.

<a id="ws-h-scenario-ws-rq-003-supported-behavior"></a>

###### Scenario: WS-RQ-003 supported behavior
- GIVEN a required fact has incomplete historical coverage
- WHEN a conditional route evaluates
- THEN no adverse fallback or fabricated first-gift determination occurs

<a id="ws-h-requirement-explicit-branch-and-join-semantics"></a>

##### Requirement: Explicit Branch and Join Semantics
Exclusive routing MUST reject overlap or unresolved alternatives. Parallel work MUST freeze selected branches and require declared source-qualified completion.

<a id="ws-h-scenario-ws-rq-004-supported-behavior"></a>

###### Scenario: WS-RQ-004 supported behavior
- GIVEN a required church reference is absent but two other references exist
- WHEN a reference join evaluates
- THEN the church-reference requirement remains unsatisfied

<a id="ws-h-requirement-versioned-publications"></a>

##### Requirement: Versioned Publications
Published executable definitions SHALL be immutable and active engagements MUST pin their publication and compatible action contracts.

<a id="ws-h-scenario-ws-rq-005-supported-behavior"></a>

###### Scenario: WS-RQ-005 supported behavior
- GIVEN an applicant is running version one
- WHEN a new template version is published
- THEN the applicant retains the old plan until an explicit authorized change

<a id="ws-h-requirement-per-run-amendments"></a>

##### Requirement: Per Run Amendments
The system SHALL support authorized individual plan amendments with an immutable impact preflight, reason, revision checks and required source review.

<a id="ws-h-scenario-ws-rq-006-supported-behavior"></a>

###### Scenario: WS-RQ-006 supported behavior
- GIVEN one applicant needs an additional interview
- WHEN a permitted amendment is committed
- THEN only that run changes and completed source history remains intact

<a id="ws-h-requirement-tenant-scoped-execution"></a>

##### Requirement: Tenant Scoped Execution
All reads, effects, events, claims and views MUST remain tenant scoped on shared infrastructure. Workflow assignment MUST NOT grant data or action authority.

<a id="ws-h-scenario-ws-rq-007-supported-behavior"></a>

###### Scenario: WS-RQ-007 supported behavior
- GIVEN a tenant member guesses another tenant run identifier
- WHEN they request its state or issue a mutation
- THEN the server denies access without exposing its existence

<a id="ws-h-requirement-runtime-current-authority"></a>

##### Requirement: Runtime Current Authority
Publication authority and runtime action authority SHALL be distinct. Current source permissions, suppression and cancellation MUST be checked at action time.

<a id="ws-h-scenario-ws-rq-008-supported-behavior"></a>

###### Scenario: WS-RQ-008 supported behavior
- GIVEN a message is queued under an old plan
- WHEN its recipient eligibility or grant is revoked
- THEN the disallowed dispatch is blocked despite the old publication

<a id="ws-h-requirement-identifier-only-orchestration"></a>

##### Requirement: Identifier Only Orchestration
Inngest events, step results, trace metadata and errors MUST contain only source-approved safe references and routing metadata, not private record contents.

<a id="ws-h-scenario-ws-rq-009-supported-behavior"></a>

###### Scenario: WS-RQ-009 supported behavior
- GIVEN an action loads a confidential application
- WHEN the action returns or fails
- THEN no application contents, signed URL or secret are stored in orchestration diagnostics

<a id="ws-h-requirement-durable-intake-and-idempotency"></a>

##### Requirement: Durable Intake and Idempotency
Accepted source events SHALL be recoverable through product-owned durable receipts/outbox and permanent semantic effect identities.

<a id="ws-h-scenario-ws-rq-010-supported-behavior"></a>

###### Scenario: WS-RQ-010 supported behavior
- GIVEN a processed gift event is delivered again after a provider dedupe window
- WHEN the workflow evaluates
- THEN the same intended business effect is not performed again

<a id="ws-h-requirement-race-safe-waiting"></a>

##### Requirement: Race Safe Waiting
Human and provider waits SHALL be satisfied from authoritative source evidence even if completion occurs before listener registration.

<a id="ws-h-scenario-ws-rq-011-supported-behavior"></a>

###### Scenario: WS-RQ-011 supported behavior
- GIVEN a reference completes before its waiting step is registered
- WHEN the durable wait is created
- THEN a source recheck recognizes completion without requiring resubmission

<a id="ws-h-requirement-uncertain-external-results"></a>

##### Requirement: Uncertain External Results
An operation that may have executed externally MUST remain outcome-unknown until reconciled and MUST NOT be blindly retried.

<a id="ws-h-scenario-ws-rq-012-supported-behavior"></a>

###### Scenario: WS-RQ-012 supported behavior
- GIVEN a provider accepts a send but the response is lost
- WHEN the execution lease or retry window expires
- THEN the operation is reconciled or reviewed rather than sent anew

<a id="ws-h-requirement-role-bound-shared-tasks"></a>

##### Requirement: Role Bound Shared Tasks
Workflow work SHALL reuse shared tasks and source-owned outcome contracts, with explicit eligible owner resolution and fallback.

<a id="ws-h-scenario-ws-rq-013-supported-behavior"></a>

###### Scenario: WS-RQ-013 supported behavior
- GIVEN no currently eligible coordinator exists
- WHEN an assignment action runs
- THEN the task enters an authorized assignment-needed queue without broadening access

<a id="ws-h-requirement-forms-and-evidence"></a>

##### Requirement: Forms and Evidence
Forms SHALL be versioned, partially savable and submitted through allowed source mappings. Evidence MUST be qualified by its owner, not inferred from upload or task status.

<a id="ws-h-scenario-ws-rq-014-supported-behavior"></a>

###### Scenario: WS-RQ-014 supported behavior
- GIVEN a required document upload is quarantined
- WHEN the requirement is evaluated
- THEN it remains unsatisfied until source-qualified clean accepted evidence exists

<a id="ws-h-requirement-external-task-access"></a>

##### Requirement: External Task Access
External access SHALL be task-purpose scoped, expiring and revocable; a GET or scanner visit MUST NOT submit, sign, approve or create membership.

<a id="ws-h-scenario-ws-rq-015-supported-behavior"></a>

###### Scenario: WS-RQ-015 supported behavior
- GIVEN an email scanner follows a reference link
- WHEN the GET is processed
- THEN no irreversible action or access grant occurs

<a id="ws-h-requirement-participant-journeys"></a>

##### Requirement: Participant Journeys
Participants SHALL see only their approved tasks, milestones, evidence and communications through server-side projections.

<a id="ws-h-scenario-ws-rq-016-supported-behavior"></a>

###### Scenario: WS-RQ-016 supported behavior
- GIVEN an applicant opens My Journey
- WHEN the server returns journey data
- THEN internal assessments, staff routing and unrelated roles are excluded from the response

<a id="ws-h-requirement-sealed-care-work"></a>

##### Requirement: Sealed Care Work
Restricted care templates, runs, memberships, counts and audit SHALL be invisible to unauthorized principals, including ordinary administrators.

<a id="ws-h-scenario-ws-rq-017-supported-behavior"></a>

###### Scenario: WS-RQ-017 supported behavior
- GIVEN a sealed intake exists
- WHEN an ordinary administrator searches or exports workflow data
- THEN no care existence signal or contents are disclosed

<a id="ws-h-requirement-governed-communication"></a>

##### Requirement: Governed Communication
All workflow communication SHALL use owning-domain purpose/audience, governed publications and the shared dispatch/history spine.

<a id="ws-h-scenario-ws-rq-018-supported-behavior"></a>

###### Scenario: WS-RQ-018 supported behavior
- GIVEN two workflows request the same acknowledgment purpose
- WHEN the requests are processed
- THEN one source semantic effect is produced or incompatible request content is explicitly blocked

<a id="ws-h-requirement-protected-domain-processes"></a>

##### Requirement: Protected Domain Processes
Finance, recurring recovery, records, identity and other protected policies SHALL remain native source-owned processes with bounded coordination hooks.

<a id="ws-h-scenario-ws-rq-019-supported-behavior"></a>

###### Scenario: WS-RQ-019 supported behavior
- GIVEN an administrator tries to create an automatic expense approval or recurring retry node
- WHEN the configuration is validated
- THEN the forbidden operation cannot be published or executed

<a id="ws-h-requirement-prospective-enrollment"></a>

##### Requirement: Prospective Enrollment
New bindings SHALL be prospective and historical imports/backfills SHALL remain side-effect-dark unless separately reviewed and authorized.

<a id="ws-h-scenario-ws-rq-020-supported-behavior"></a>

###### Scenario: WS-RQ-020 supported behavior
- GIVEN legacy contribution history is imported
- WHEN a donor welcome workflow is active
- THEN historical records do not trigger outward welcomes automatically

<a id="ws-h-requirement-scheduling-semantics"></a>

##### Requirement: Scheduling Semantics
Timers SHALL preserve timezone, time interpretation and calendar policy. Pause, expiry, late evidence and catch-up MUST have explicit nonapproval behavior.

<a id="ws-h-scenario-ws-rq-021-supported-behavior"></a>

###### Scenario: WS-RQ-021 supported behavior
- GIVEN a run pauses with a relative reminder and fixed document expiry
- WHEN time passes
- THEN the relative clock pauses where allowed while fixed expiry follows its source rule

<a id="ws-h-requirement-simulation"></a>

##### Requirement: Simulation
Simulation SHALL use the production evaluator with synthetic or separately authorized fixtures and no live side effects.

<a id="ws-h-scenario-ws-rq-022-supported-behavior"></a>

###### Scenario: WS-RQ-022 supported behavior
- GIVEN a draft is tested
- WHEN its message and access nodes execute in simulation
- THEN only simulated outcomes occur and no provider credentials or live recipients are used

<a id="ws-h-requirement-accessible-editing"></a>

##### Requirement: Accessible Editing
The complete authoring and participant experience SHALL target WCAG 2.2 AA and include a usable keyboard/outline alternative to the canvas.

<a id="ws-h-scenario-ws-rq-023-supported-behavior"></a>

###### Scenario: WS-RQ-023 supported behavior
- GIVEN staff uses only keyboard and assistive technology
- WHEN they configure, validate and publish a permitted rule
- THEN all required actions and errors are usable without dragging nodes

<a id="ws-h-requirement-safe-concurrency"></a>

##### Requirement: Safe Concurrency
Concurrent edits and source completions SHALL be serialized through revision checks and unique source effects, not last-writer overwrite.

<a id="ws-h-scenario-ws-rq-024-supported-behavior"></a>

###### Scenario: WS-RQ-024 supported behavior
- GIVEN two source completions reach one join simultaneously
- WHEN both attempt to advance the run
- THEN one accepted transition preserves both evidence facts

<a id="ws-h-requirement-controlled-rollout-and-recovery"></a>

##### Requirement: Controlled Rollout and Recovery
Disabling optional enrollment or losing the executor SHALL preserve valid source records, durable accepted work and manual recovery.

<a id="ws-h-scenario-ws-rq-025-supported-behavior"></a>

###### Scenario: WS-RQ-025 supported behavior
- GIVEN Inngest becomes unavailable
- WHEN a source event is durably accepted
- THEN work remains recoverable and essential source operations do not depend on a custom template

<a id="ws-h-requirement-source-ready-catalog"></a>

##### Requirement: Source Ready Catalog
Each capability pack SHALL activate only when its source commands, privacy projections and providers are qualified.

<a id="ws-h-scenario-ws-rq-026-supported-behavior"></a>

###### Scenario: WS-RQ-026 supported behavior
- GIVEN automated signing lacks a certified source adapter
- WHEN a tenant attempts activation
- THEN the lane stays unavailable and any valid manual evidence path is labeled honestly

<a id="ws-h-requirement-template-portability"></a>

##### Requirement: Template Portability
Exported templates SHALL contain no live credentials, person/run data or executable scripts; imports SHALL be inert drafts requiring tenant rebinding.

<a id="ws-h-scenario-ws-rq-027-supported-behavior"></a>

###### Scenario: WS-RQ-027 supported behavior
- GIVEN a portable template is imported
- WHEN its foreign source references are inspected
- THEN unsafe content is rejected and valid content cannot execute before binding and publication

<a id="ws-h-requirement-contract-upgrade-compatibility"></a>

##### Requirement: Contract Upgrade Compatibility
Runtime deployments SHALL preserve compatible source action behavior for active publications or require controlled migration.

<a id="ws-h-scenario-ws-rq-028-supported-behavior"></a>

###### Scenario: WS-RQ-028 supported behavior
- GIVEN an action implementation changes incompatibly
- WHEN an old run advances
- THEN it uses a supported compatible contract or stops safely for migration

<a id="ws-h-requirement-restore-and-retention-safety"></a>

##### Requirement: Restore and Retention Safety
Restore and disposal processes SHALL preserve source authority, revocations and necessary lawful dedupe evidence; restore MUST NOT reactivate outward effects blindly.

<a id="ws-h-scenario-ws-rq-029-supported-behavior"></a>

###### Scenario: WS-RQ-029 supported behavior
- GIVEN a backup predates a confirmed send and revoked grant
- WHEN the system restores
- THEN dispatch remains contained until effects and permissions reconcile

<a id="ws-h-requirement-ai-has-no-additional-authority"></a>

##### Requirement: AI Has No Additional Authority
AI assistance SHALL remain subject to the same catalog, data purposes, validation, simulation and human publication rules.

<a id="ws-h-scenario-ws-rq-030-supported-behavior"></a>

###### Scenario: WS-RQ-030 supported behavior
- GIVEN an assistant proposes a workflow requiring forbidden data or action
- WHEN the proposal is checked
- THEN normal authority checks reject it and no privileged effect occurs

<a id="ws-h-repository-relative-artifact-openspec-changes-add-workflow-studio-specs-platform-surfaces-spec-md"></a>

#### Repository-relative artifact: `openspec/changes/add-workflow-studio/specs/platform-surfaces/spec.md`

<a id="ws-h-platform-surfaces-participant-journeys"></a>

### Platform surfaces — participant journeys

<a id="ws-h-added-requirements-2"></a>

#### ADDED Requirements

<a id="ws-h-requirement-authenticated-participant-journey-experience"></a>

##### Requirement: Authenticated Participant Journey Experience

The platform SHALL provide an authenticated, purpose-scoped My Journey experience for applicants and other approved workflow participants, implemented within an existing application surface without creating a second staff console. A participant mode in the missionary application MUST NOT imply missionary, donor, financial, or unrestricted CRM privileges. Mission Control remains the authoring, administration and operational-depth owner. Public entry forms may originate on the tenant website; private journey records and evidence MUST NOT become public content.

<a id="ws-h-scenario-applicant-follows-their-next-step"></a>

###### Scenario: Applicant follows their next step

- GIVEN a person has explicitly authorized access to their application journey
- WHEN they open My Journey in participant mode
- THEN they see permitted tasks, milestones, requested evidence and source-safe communications
- AND they cannot enumerate staff graphs, other candidates, confidential assessments, care cases, or unrelated missionary/donor information

<a id="ws-h-scenario-one-person-holds-several-roles"></a>

###### Scenario: One person holds several roles

- GIVEN a person is both a donor and an applicant in the same tenant
- WHEN they navigate between self-service experiences
- THEN each experience resolves its own current permissions and source projections
- AND neither role implicitly grants privileges belonging to the other

### 14. Local verification report

> **Integration note:** This is the original September 12 report. New local rerun results appear separately in [Verification](#verification). Neither report is Core implementation, database, browser, provider or deployment evidence.


<a id="ws-h-local-specification-verification-report"></a>

### Local specification verification report

**Date:** September 12, 2026. **Repository research baseline:** `7abd2c11ffd4ed70c6775c4fd6f51c996e4350dd`.

<a id="ws-h-executed-checks"></a>

#### Executed checks

| Suite | Checks | Passed | Failed |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Structural/referential fixture checks (`verify-spec.mjs`) | 34 | 34 | 0 |
| JSON Schema 2020-12 and negative fixtures (`validate-schemas.py`) | 29 | 29 | 0 |
| **Total local artifact checks** | **63** | **63** | **0** |

The structural checks ran with Node v22.16.0; JSON Schema checks used Python's `jsonschema` 4.26.0. The scripts are local specification-verification helpers, not additions to Core's runtime. Machine-readable per-check results are stored alongside this report.

<a id="ws-h-verified-artifact-coverage"></a>

#### Verified artifact coverage

- 96 unique workflow recipes across eight persona-oriented packs, each disabled by default and carrying explicit protected boundaries, evidence and prerequisites.
- 16 inert workflow reference definitions with declared triggers, bound aliases, unique node IDs, valid stages, valid parallel references and no recursive subflows.
- 4 inert form reference definitions with source mappings, versioning and valid conditional field references.
- 26 unique proposed implementation tickets with valid acyclic dependencies and known acceptance references.
- 352 unique test specifications: 64 cross-cutting scenarios and three per workflow recipe. All retain `specified_not_executed` status.
- Three JSON Schema contracts are structurally valid; all supplied workflow/form instances pass their respective schemas.
- Negative fixtures reject enabled reference workflows, unknown executable fields, raw form mappings, missing roles, duplicate node IDs, invalid stage references, absent recipes, historical execution, retry-safe unknown outcomes and confirmed outcomes without source evidence.

<a id="ws-h-what-these-results-do-not-prove"></a>

#### What these results do not prove

The checks do not implement or validate a production workflow interpreter. Full static type/dominance analysis, source purpose/permission binding, database race behavior, current source API compatibility, real recipient projections, end-to-end application flows, accessibility compliance, performance and provider semantics remain implementation gates.

No Core runtime, database migration, source adapter, actual Resend message, Inngest execution, repository test suite, browser acceptance test, or pinned OpenSpec CLI validation was run in this task. The 352 acceptance-test specifications are requirements for later automated/manual tests, not 352 passing product tests. The OpenSpec changes remain proposed and unarchived.

<a id="ws-h-reproduce-local-checks"></a>

#### Reproduce local checks

From the extracted package root, run `node verification/verify-spec.mjs` (or Bun's equivalent) and `python verification/validate-schemas.py` in an environment with jsonschema installed. The helpers rewrite only their local result JSON files. Integrating the specification into Core requires the repository's own pinned CLI, source-aware checks and review described in the README.

<a id="web-h-asym-web-studio"></a>

### Asym Web Studio
<a id="web-h-hybrid-authoring-workflows-and-automation-full-proposed-build-specification"></a>

#### Hybrid authoring, workflows and automation — full proposed build specification

**Research date:** September 12, 2026  

**Change ID:** `add-web-studio-hybrid-authoring`  

**Status:** Complete proposed specification; owner amendments not yet recorded in Core. Not implemented or production-qualified.

Visual-first creation, ministry-controlled custom source, and mixed developer/editor workflows share one CMS contract and publication process. Payload stays private. No mandatory browser IDE, hosted AI or help-desk model.

**Package:** 18 user workflows · 12 fixed automations · 48 requirements · 96 specified implementation scenarios · 27 implementation slices · 50 evidence entries.  

**Local validation:** 48 structural/reference tests and 378 specification consistency checks passed. These are not Core runtime tests.

The proposal identifies HA-A1–HA-A4 that require explicit adoption. Detailed limits and component grammar are proposed design choices, not previously ratified facts. Current source, unmerged intent, official technology facts and qualification unknowns are distinguished in the evidence register.

<a id="web-overview"></a>

### Asym Web Studio — Hybrid Authoring Specification Package

> **Integration note:** This complete source package supplies Phase 42 detail. HA-A1–HA-A4 remain explicit implementation-adoption decisions; the roadmap already assigns their delivery, but this compilation does not claim they were merged into Core. Native Phase 23 work remains independent. See [IG-08](#ig-08).


**Version:** 1.0 · **Research date:** September 12, 2026  

**Proposed change:** `add-web-studio-hybrid-authoring`  

**Status:** Complete draft specification package for adoption and implementation planning. Not merged, dispatched, implemented, deployed, or runtime-qualified.

<a id="web-h-the-product"></a>

#### The product

One Asym-owned Web Studio lets staff build and maintain websites visually while developers deliver custom presentation from ministry-controlled source repositories. Payload stays private behind Asym operations. Both paths use the same semantic content, compatible presentation contracts, preview evidence, and existing publication authority.

“Workflows and automation” here means the editorial, visual-composition, developer-delivery, publication, and recovery workflows of Web Studio. It does not mean rebuilding the general Workflow Studio, Support Hub, CRM, or a hosted coding platform.

<a id="web-h-four-decisions-to-adopt-explicitly"></a>

#### Four decisions to adopt explicitly

**HA-A1 — Hybrid composition.** Add a versioned, bounded Page composition profile with Stack, Split and Grid containers and declared safe visual settings. Preserve flat v1 documents and Article constraints. Do not turn content into arbitrary CSS or executable source.

**HA-A2 — Ministry-controlled source.** Support verified, ministry-controlled custom Presentation Package repositories and named authorized maintainers. Source authorship does not grant platform admission, production-data access, or publication authority.

**HA-A3 — Visual adapter and origins.** Qualify Puck core as the leading composition adapter, with Asym-owned forms, canonical documents and commands. Run qualified custom composer content on a separate origin; unreviewed source is never loaded into staff authoring. No paid Puck AI/Cloud or Payload enterprise editor dependency.

**HA-A4 — Governed delivery.** Connect exact source capture and independent builds to the existing D1/D9/D10/D25 publication owners. This does not add a blanket approval step to content paths already allowed by tenant policy.

These are proposed amendment IDs local to this package, not allocated Core ADR numbers. Existing D1–D36 are not silently rewritten.

<a id="web-h-starting-proof"></a>

#### Starting proof

A staff member builds a meaningful page visually. A developer redesigns its presentation in the ministry repository using ordinary tools. The qualified design is reviewed and activated through Asym. The staff member then changes text, images and supported layouts without GitHub. Concurrent edits, stale approvals and failed builds do not lose acknowledged work or mix public generations.

<a id="web-h-what-has-actually-been-checked"></a>

#### What has actually been checked

Current repository files, relevant governing/active contracts, selected tickets, and current official product documentation were inspected. The accompanying validator tests example structural contracts and specification traceability only. Actual Supabase/Payload atomicity, Puck/Next integration, browser isolation, production capacity and end-to-end behavior remain mandatory implementation qualification gates. See [evidence](#web-evidence) and [validation](#web-validation).

No Core files, GitHub issues, branches, migrations, deployments, user accounts, or provider connections were changed. The `baseline/` document is the recovered user direction, not an instruction to preserve the superseded support-oriented draft.
